caption: [Community heroes responding to a vehicle fire]On 21 June 2025 at about 8:55pm, Mr Muhammad Tashir Bin Mansor was resting at home after his duty shift as a firefighter with Changi Airport Groups Airport Emergency Services when he heard a fire alarm from a multi-storey carpark (MSCP) at 635A, Pasir Ris Drive 1. Looking out the window, Mr Tashir saw black smoke from the MSCP and immediately dashed out of his home to help.At the same time, Ms Nur Fatin Binte Raihan, Ms Nur Sakinah Binte Abdul Rahman and Ms Julia Sarah Binte Muhammad Hasan who were at a nearby void deck also saw the black smoke. Ms Julia promptly called 995 and the three ladies also made their way to the MSCP. Upon reaching the MSCP, Mr Tashir spotted a car on fire on the second floor. With the assistance of Ms Julia and Ms Sakinah, Mr Tashir used a nearby hosereel to contain the car fire, while Ms Fatin helped to alert other members of public to stay away.The speedy and courageous actions of the four individuals prevented the fire from spreading.On 8 July 2025, the four Community First Responders were presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award. The award was presented by COL Ser Boon Hui, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division.You too can make a difference during an emergency by downloading the SCDF myResponder app and registering as a Community First Responder via the app. You can also learn essential lifesaving skills through SCDFs Responder Plus Programme at go.gov.sg/scdfrpp. Lets build ANationOfLifesavers together!CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRoleFrom L to R Ms Nur Fatin Binte Raihan; Ms Nur Sakinah Binte Abdul Rahman; Ms Julia Sarah Binte Muhammad Hasan; COL Ser Boon Hui, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division; Mr Muhammad Tashir Bin Mansor

caption: [Height Rescue Operation @ 250 North Bridge Road]Earlier today at about 11:20am, SCDF responded to a height rescue incident involving two workers who were stranded on a gondola between the 28th and 29th floor of a building at the abovementioned location.Upon arrival, firefighters immediately checked on the gondola's stability, as well as the condition of the workers on the gondola.Rescuers from the Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) also responded to the scene and set up the rescue equipment at level 30 and level 29. The gondola was then secured with safety lines, before a DART rescuer descended onto the gondola to rescue the two workers. The DART rescuer secured the two workers who were wearing body harnesses, and brought them into the building through the windows on level 29 and level 30.Both workers were assessed by an SCDF paramedic and conveyed to Raffles Hospital in a stable condition.

caption: [Fire @ Block 194 Kim Keat Avenue]Earlier this morning at about 11:50am, SCDF responded to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon arrival, one of the bedrooms in a 12th-floor unit was on fire. Firefighters entered the smoke-filled unit and extinguished the fire with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit as well as the corridor area outside the unit sustained heat and smoke damage.Three persons had evacuated from the affected unit before SCDF's arrival. As a precautionary measure, about 60 persons from the block were evacuated by the Police.Two persons from the affected unit were assessed by SCDF for smoke inhalation. One of them was conveyed to KK Womens and Childrens Hospital while the other person declined to be sent to the hospital.Preliminary findings indicate that the cause of the fire is likely from an electrical origin in the affected bedroom.To prevent such fires, SCDF would like to remind the public:a) Do not overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off appliances when they are not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Frayed wires or cracked cords should be replaced or repaired immediately;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces;e) Use only appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at Do not leave batteries or devices charging unattended for an extended period of time, or leave it charging overnight.
cleaned_caption: [Fire @ Block 194 Kim Keat Avenue] Earlier this morning at about 11:50am, SCDF responded to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, one of the bedrooms in a 12th-floor unit was on fire. Firefighters entered the smoke-filled unit and extinguished the fire with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit as well as the corridor area outside the unit sustained heat and smoke damage. Three persons had evacuated from the affected unit before SCDF's arrival. As a precautionary measure, about 60 persons from the block were evacuated by the Police. Two persons from the affected unit were assessed by SCDF for smoke inhalation. One of them was conveyed to KK Women's and Children's Hospital while the other person declined to be sent to the hospital. Preliminary findings indicate that the cause of the fire is likely from an electrical origin in the affected bedroom. To prevent such fires, SCDF would like to remind the public: a) Do not overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances; b) Always switch off appliances when they are not in use; c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Frayed wires or cracked cords should be replaced or repaired immediately; d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces; e) Use only appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at. Do not leave batteries or devices charging unattended for an extended period of time, or leave it charging overnight.

Mr Edwin Tong, Minister for Law and Second Minister for Home Affairs, graced the ceremony as the Guest of Honour. His wife, Mrs Tong, served as the Lady Patron for the symbolic christening and official induction of the Blue Dolphin into service. Operating from West Coast Marine Fire Station, the Blue Dolphin enhances SCDF's coverage and readiness in Singapore's waters. The MRV2G comes with some key enhancements: - Integrated Command Post to enhance command and control during major incidents- Advanced Navigational System for precise vessel handling - Launch and Recovery System for improved deployment of the Rigid Hull Inflatable Boat during marine firefighting and search and rescue operations- Solar charging system and biofuel-compatible engines for better sustainabilityJointly developed by the SCDF, HTX (Home Team Science and Technology Agency), Defence Science and Technology Agency (DSTA), and Penguin Shipyard International, the MRV2G exemplifies SCDFs commitment to meeting current and future maritime emergency challenges.

caption: [Marine Firefighting Operation @ East of Singapore]This morning (20 June) at about 8:10am, SCDF was alerted to a fire onboard an oil tanker anchored in the waters of Singapores eastern area.Three SCDF marine rescue vessels and about 40 marine firefighting specialists from Brani Marine Fire Station and West Coast Marine Fire Station were deployed to the incident. Upon SCDFs arrival, black smoke was seen emitting from a storeroom in the oil tanker. Marine firefighters used a water monitor from a marine rescue vessel to cool the exterior of the affected oil tanker. Known as boundary cooling, this helps to cool the metal structure of vessels. Concurrently, another team of firefghters boarded the oil tanker to locate the seat of fire and extinguished it using a water jet. There were no reported injuries and all crew members of the affected oil tanker were accounted for. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

caption: [Fire @ Block 5, Holland Close] Earlier this evening at about 7:25pm, firefighters from Alexandra Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, one of the bedrooms in a 23rd-floor unit was on fire. Firefighters entered the smoke-filled unit and extinguished the fire with two water jets. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit also sustained heat and smoke damage. Two persons who had evacuated from the affected unit before SCDF's arrival were assessed for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital. About 100 persons were evacuated by the Police and SCDF from the affected block. During the firefighting operation, two firefighters experienced heat exhaustion. One was conveyed to Singapore General Hospital and the other to National University Hospital. Both of them were conscious when conveyed to the hospitals.The cause of the fire is under investigation.*Update: One of the firefighters was discharged from the hospital earlier this morning (20 June) and given five days of medical leave. The other firefighter has been warded for further observation. SCDF will continue to check on their well-being.**Update: The second firefighter was discharged earlier today and was given 4 days of medical leave. Both firefighters are currently resting at home.

caption: [Keeping Singapore Safe | Fire Safety Managers]Since 1994, with the passing of the Fire Safety (Fire Safety Manager) Regulations Act, public and industrial buildings in Singapore (such as those with high occupancy or specific risk profiles) are required to appoint a Fire Safety Manager (FSM). Today, there are around 15,000 certified FSMs in Singapore. Working closely with building owners, the key role of FSMs is to ensure compliance with the Fire Safety Act and its regulations in the building premises the FSM is appointed to. FSMs also help to enhance the safety of building occupants by raising their fire safety awareness and emergency preparedness through fire drills and implementing fire prevention measures in the building premises.As SCDFs key point-of-contact on fire safety matters, FSMs provide essential building information and help facilitate SCDFs emergency response, as well as the evacuation of the building occupants during an emergency. Their fire safety training and expertise make them a vital partner in keeping building premises and communities fire-safe.Swipe through to meet two experienced FSMs: Ms Veronica Mah from National University Hospital and Mr Ibrahim Bin Daud from Singapore Sports Hub!

caption: [Fire @ 20, Jalan Tenteram]At about 11:40am today, firefighters from Central Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire involved items placed along the corridor outside a unit on the 2nd floor and 3rd floor. The fire had also affected the inside of both these units. The fire was extinguished by SCDF using two water jets. As a result of the fire, a few neighboring units also sustained heat and soot damage.About 40 persons from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. SCDF conveyed two persons to Singapore General Hospital, two persons to Tan Tock Seng Hospital, and one person to KK Womens and Childrens Hospital for smoke inhalation.The cause of the fire is under investigation.Members of the public are advised to help maintain a safe living environment by keeping common corridors, lift lobbies, and staircases free of clutter. A cluttered corridor can increase the risk of fire spread, hinder evacuation efforts, and delay SCDFs response during an emergency. Find out more on the guidelines on the use of common areas. SCDF conveyed five persons to the hospital for smoke inhalation. One of them, a 51-year-old man, was subsequently arrested by the police for the offence of mischief by fire.Preliminary findings by SCDF indicate that the fire was intentionally started.

caption: [Fire @ Block 226, Lorong 8 Toa Payoh] Yesterday (14 May) at about 10:50pm, firefighters from Bishan Fire Station responded to a fire at Block 226, Lorong 8 Toa Payoh.Upon arrival, the living room of a 10th floor unit was on fire. Firefighters conducted forcible entry into the smoke-filled unit and extinguished the fire with a water jet.During the firefighting operation, firefighters found a person inside a bedroom. The person was brought out to safety and assessed by a paramedic for smoke inhalation and burn injuries. The person was conveyed to Singapore General Hospital. About 30 persons from the neighbouring units were evacuated by the Police and SCDF.A person from a unit on the 14th floor who had experienced breathlessness was conveyed to Tan Tock Seng Hospital.Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from a personal mobility device (PMD) battery in the living room. To prevent such fires, SCDF would like to remind the public not to purchase or use non-original batteries for their active mobility devices, including PMDs and powered assisted bicycles (PABs). Also, do not charge PMD/PAB batteries for an extended period of time or overnight. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

caption: [SCDF Day @ Civil Defence Academy]Yesterday evening, the SCDF Day Dining-In ceremony was held at the Civil Defence Academy. This annual event commemorates the integration of the Singapore Fire Service and SCDF on 15 April 1989, consolidating Singapores fire, rescue and emergency medical services response into a single organisation.The ceremony, which serves as a platform for our officers to rededicate their commitment to our lifesaving mission and reaffirm our core values of Pride and Care, was attended by SCDF regular officers, full-time National Servicemen, Operationally Ready National Servicemen and civilian staff. Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS), Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, graced the event as the Guest of Honour. In his speech, MOS Faishal recognised and commended SCDF personnel who have exemplified SCDFs core values in and beyond their duties. He also spoke about SCDFs Operation Lionheart contingent, who were recently deployed to Myanmar for disaster relief efforts, and praised the team for their professionalism, compassion and dedication to saving lives. Congratulations to all award winners! As we honour their achievements, we also reaffirm our dedication and commitment towards our mission to protect and save lives and property. caption: [Update 9: Operation Lionhearts Homecoming] Earlier today (8 April) at about 4pm, the SCDFs Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent returned to Singapore. The OLH contingent, comprising 80 members and four search canines, was deployed to support search and rescue efforts in Myanmar on 29 March, a day after the country was hit by the devastating earthquake. A welcome reception was held at Changi Airport, where Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, and Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development received the contingent members. Families and loved ones were also present to warmly welcome them home. In his welcome address, Minister Shanmugam expressed his heartfelt gratitude to the OLH contingent, along with officers from the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX), for assisting with search and rescue operations in Myanmar. He commended the contingent for their dedication to service. Minister Shanmugam also expressed his appreciation to the families and loved ones of the contingent members for their support. To our OLH contingent, you have truly embodied the spirit of being a Lifesaver, not only in Singapore but also beyond borders. Welcome home, our Lifesavers We would like to express our utmost appreciation to the Singapore Embassy in Yangon for facilitating the OLH contingents deployment in Myanmar. We would also like to thank Singapore Airlines, Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore, Changi Airport Group, Myanmar Airways International, ST Logistics and SATS Ltd Singapore Hub team for facilitating the contingents flight and logistical arrangements on short notice. The people of Myanmar will always be in our hearts and minds. Though the road to recovery may be challenging, their admirable resilience in the face of adversity will guide them through, and we are confident that they will emerge stronger and recover from this disaster.

caption: [Fire @ 278, River Valley Road] Earlier today at about 9:45am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at 278, River Valley Road.Upon arrival, the fire was raging on the second and third floors of a 3-storey shophouse. Several persons were on a ledge outside the third-floor unit. Members of the public, including construction workers, used a metal scaffolding and a ladder to reach those stranded and brought a number of them to safety. SCDF immediately deployed rescue ladders and a Combined Platform Ladder to rescue the rest of the stranded persons on the ledge. At the same time, firefighters proceeded to the second and third floor to fight the fire. The fire was extinguished with three water jets within 30 minutes.About 80 persons from the affected shophouse and nearby premises were evacuated by the Police and SCDF.A total of 18 casualties (four adults and 14 children) were conveyed to the hospital. The cause of the fire is under investigation.We would like to thank the members of the public who assisted in the rescue of the stranded persons for their quick actions and bravery.

caption: [Update 8: Stand down of Operation Lionheart in Myanmar] The 80-member Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent has begun preparations to return home. Over the last two days, the OLH contingent has been handing over essential supplies such as tents, canned food and ready-to-eat rations, to the Myanmar Fire Services Department (MFSD). The OLH contingent also donated two tents to Naypyidaw Womens Hospital, and five tents along with medical drugs and medical supplies to Naypyidaw General Hospital. It is hoped that these supplies will continue to help the relief and recovery efforts as the people of Myanmar work to rebuild their community. On behalf of SCDF, Team Leader COL Tay Zhi Wei, gifted a battery-operated hydraulic cutter to U Myat Thu, Director General MFSD. This cutter was instrumental in rescuing a man trapped underneath concrete slabs in a semi-collapsed three-storey residential building on 30 March. Despite its compact size, the cutters powerful capability enabled it to cut through the rebar in the concrete slabs within an extremely confined area, freeing the man and saving his life. This cutter is now an enduring symbol of friendship between the SCDF and MFSD, where it will continue to serve, saving lives in the good hands of MFSD. An appreciation ceremony organised by the National Disaster Management Committee (NDMC) in Naypyidaw, brought together Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) teams from Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Vietnam and Philippines. A moment of silence was observed in memory of the earthquake victims. The OLH contingent will be returning home tomorrow (8 April) at 4:10pm, on Singapore Airlines at Changi Airport Terminal 3.

caption: [SCDFs Operation Lionheart Deployment to Myanmar]In response to the request for humanitarian assistance in the aftermath of an earthquake in Myanmar yesterday (28 Mar), SCDF has deployed the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent to assist in disaster rescue efforts. The contingent departed from Changi Airport at about 1:20pm today (29 Mar).Led by Team Leader, COL Tay Zhi Wei, the 80-member OLH contingent comprises rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS), full-time National Servicemen medical doctors, paramedics, search specialists with four canines, hazardous materials specialists, and support officers. The pre-departure briefing and preparation began early this morning at HQ SCDF. The OLH contingent is carrying an array of portable Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) equipment such as cutting, breaking and lifting equipment, as well as life detection devices and fibre-optic scopes. These equipment which are battery operated will allow the team to be swiftly deployed to affected areas to begin immediate USAR operations. In addition, three SCDF officers are also deployed to Myanmar as part of the ASEAN Emergency Response and Assessment Team (ERAT) under the auspices of the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management (AHA Centre). The ASEAN-ERATs primary function is to provide rapid assessment and determine the critical resources required for the areas affected by the earthquake. Prior to the contingents departure, Associate Professor , Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development met with the team at HQ SCDF to express his appreciation to the officers and to see them off, together with their family and loved ones.We would like to thank for facilitating the flight arrangements on short notice, especially during such major disasters where prompt assistance is crucial to those in need. We would also like to thank and SATS Ltd Singapore Hub team for their assistance.We wish our OLH contingent a safe and successful mission.

The contingent departed from Changi Airport at about 1:20pm today (29 Mar).Led by Team Leader, COL Tay Zhi Wei, the 80-member OLH contingent comprises rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS), full-time National Servicemen medical doctors, paramedics, search specialists with four canines, hazardous materials specialists, and support officers. The pre-departure briefing and preparation began early this morning at HQ SCDF. The OLH contingent is carrying an array of portable Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) equipment such as cutting, breaking and lifting equipment, as well as life detection devices and fibre-optic scopes. These equipment which are battery operated will allow the team to be swiftly deployed to affected areas to begin immediate USAR operations. In addition, three SCDF officers are also deployed to Myanmar as part of the ASEAN Emergency Response and Assessment Team (ERAT) under the auspices of the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management (AHA Centre). The ASEAN-ERATs primary function is to provide rapid assessment and determine the critical resources required for the areas affected by the earthquake. Prior to the contingents departure, Associate Professor , Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development met with the team at HQ SCDF to express his appreciation to the officers and to see them off, together with their family and loved ones.We would like to thank for facilitating the flight arrangements on short notice, especially during such major disasters where prompt assistance is crucial to those in need. We would also like to thank and SATS Ltd Singapore Hub team for their assistance.We wish our OLH contingent a safe and successful mission.

caption: [Responders, Partners and Volunteers Appreciation Event 2025]On Tuesday (18 Feb), the Responders, Partners and Volunteers Appreciation Event was held at HomeTeamNS Khatib.The event, jointly organised by the Ministry of Home Affairs and SCDF, recognises SGSecure Responders, SCDF Community First Responders (CFRs) and SCDF volunteers who have helped save lives and property, as well as community partners who have played a significant role in building the pool of Responders.Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS), Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, graced the event as the Guest of Honour.In his speech, MOS Faishal highlighted the Lifesavers Emergency Point (LEP) initiative, a joint effort between SCDF, Temasek Foundation, the Housing Development Board and Town Councils, in strengthening the communitys readiness towards emergencies. Situated at the lift lobbies of HDB blocks, these LEPs are equipped with Automated External Defibrillators and fire extinguishers for public use. Since 2023, over 4,000 fire extinguishers have been installed across one in every two HDB blocks. These fire extinguishes have already been used in more than 70 minor fire incidents.During the event, 27 Responders received appreciation plaques for their contributions towards saving lives. 52 community partners, including all 17 Town Councils, were recognised for their partnership with the Home Team to strengthen emergency preparedness initiatives. 26 SCDF Volunteers comprising Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit Exemplary Officers, National Civil Defence Cadet Corps Honorary Officers and Senior Cadet Lieutenants as well as Civil Defence Lionhearter Clubs were also presented appreciation plaques for their dedication and efforts.Thank you to all our Responders, volunteers and community partners! We look forward to the continued collaboration in empowering the community to step forward to help during emergencies.CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversANationofLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRoleSGSecure

caption: [SCDF Annual Statistics 2024] The SCDF annual statistics for Emergency Medical Services (EMS), Fire Incidents, and Fire Safety Enforcement Checks for Year 2024 were released today.Key takeaways: 1 SCDF responded to 245,279 EMS calls in 2024, a decrease of 0.6% or 1,553 calls from 2023. While demand for SCDFs EMS has alleviated slightly, we are observing a general upwards trend over the past five years. The increase in demand is expected to continue beyond 2025, given the ageing population in Singapore. 2 The overall number of fire calls increased by 1.8% to 1,990 calls in 2024. 3 There were 968 fires in residential premises in 2024, a decrease of 0.2% from 2023. Fires due to unattended cooking and electrical origin remained the top two causes of fires in residential premises in 2024. 4 There were 67 fires involving Active Mobility Devices (AMDs) in 2024, an increase of 21.8% or 12 calls from 2023. AMD fires remain an area of concern especially for those that occur at residential premises. 5 SCDF stepped up the number of fire safety enforcement checks in 2024, with a total of 15,075 fire safety enforcement checks conducted. caption: [Rescue Incident @ 11 Toa Payoh Industrial Park]Earlier today, at approximately 5:50pm, SCDF was alerted to an incident at 11 Toa Payoh Industrial Park. A few persons were reportedly trapped under piles of rugs after a mezzanine, along with storage racks, collapsed inside a warehouse unit on the first floor.One person had managed to free himself before SCDF arrived and informed that three other persons were still trapped.Firefighters from Bishan Fire Station, rescuers from the Special Response Unit and the Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) commenced a search within the affected area, measuring approximately 20 meters by 10 metres. SCDF search dogs were also deployed. The firefighters and rescuers removed piles of rugs and cut through storage racks to reach the three trapped persons. After an operation lasting about 90 minutes, all three persons, two of whom were children, were rescued. Two persons were conveyed to Tan Tock Seng Hospital, while the two children were taken to KK Women's and Children's Hospital. All four persons were conscious when conveyed to the hospitals.

caption: [Fire @ Blk 224A, Sumang Lane]Earlier this morning at about 5:05am, firefighters from Punggol Fire Station, SengKang Fire Station and Tampines Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, black smoke was emitting from a unit on the seventh floor. The fire, which involved a bedroom, was extinguished with a water jet. Four persons had evacuated from the unit before SCDFs arrival. About 60 persons from the neighbouring units were evacuated by the police and SCDF as a precautionary measure.A person was assessed by an SCDF paramedic for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital.Preliminary findings indicate that the fire was likely caused by an electrical origin in the bedroom. SCDF would like to remind the public to adopt the following good practices to prevent electrical fires:a) Do not overload power sockets with electrical appliances;b) Switch off electrical appliances when not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Frayed wires should be replaced or repaired immediately; d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces; e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at Do not leave batteries or devices to charge unattended for an extended period of time or leave it charging overnight.

caption: [SCDF Fire Safety Enforcement Blitz]Yesterday, SCDF conducted a fire safety enforcement blitz as part of its ongoing efforts to maintain a high level of fire safety standards in buildings and premises.During the inspection, there were several fire safety non-compliances detected at two commercial premises. These non-compliances include the non-maintenance of fire safety provisions such as exit lights, fire extinguishers and hosereels, and obstructions to emergency escape routes due to poor housekeeping. There were also unauthorised fire safety works involving installation of partitions and unauthorised change of use such as the conversion of a carpark space to a storage area without approval in one of the premises.Enforcement actions will be taken against the responsible entities for the various non-compliances.SCDF will continue to step up enforcement checks at premises where increased footfall is expected amidst the festive season. Premises owners are reminded to practice good housekeeping and adhere to the fire safety regulations, so as to ensure the safety of everyone.

caption: [Fire @ Blk 921 Tampines Street 91]At about 9:40pm today (24 Dec), firefighters from Tampines Fire Station and Changi Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, black smoke was emitting from a unit on the first floor. The fire, which involved a bedroom inside the unit, was extinguished with a water jet. There was no one inside the unit. About 50 residents from neighbouring units were evacuated by the SCDF and the police as a precautionary measure.No ambulance assistance was required. Preliminary findings indicate that the fire had likely originated from a Power Assisted Bicycle (PAB) battery which was charging inside the bedroom. To prevent such fires, the public is reminded not to leave batteries or devices charging for a prolonged period or leave them charging unattended. In addition, do not purchase or use non-original batteries for your active mobility devices.

caption: [SMRT Trains staff commended for extinguishing a fire] On 9 October 2024 at about 9am, Trains staff at Marsiling MRT Station were alerted by members of the public to a fire near Block 162 Woodlands Street 13. Without hesitation, Assistant Station Manager Umme Safiyah Binte N Syed Pulavar and Senior Station Manager Nor Haqeem SapiI Kasamin retrieved a fire extinguisher and proceeded to the incident location. Upon their arrival, two bicycles parked at the void deck were on fire. While Safiyah assisted with crowd control and ensured the safety of onlookers, Haqeem used the fire extinguisher to put out the fire. In recognition of their public-spiritedness, the SCDF Community First Responder Award was presented to Safiyah and Haqeem on 22 November 2024. The awards were presented by COL Bob Tan, Deputy Commander, 4th SCDF Division. Over the last five years, more than 130 Community Lifesaver Awards and Community First Responder Awards have been presented to staff from SMRT Trains. You too can make a difference during an emergency. caption: [SCDF-ITE Memorandum of Understanding Signing and Launch of the Work-Study Diploma in Paramedicine ] Earlier today (19 Nov), a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was signed between the SCDF and the , marking a strategic partnership that provides Work-Study Diploma opportunities for aspiring trainees to join the Life Saving Force. Following the MOU signing, the new Work-Study Diploma (WSDip) in Paramedicine was officially launched. Developed in collaboration with the ITE and other industry partners, this programme provides a unique opportunity for aspiring trainees to kickstart their careers with the SCDF while pursuing a nationally recognised diploma. With a dynamic curriculum, the programme equips trainees with advanced medical knowledge and skills for handling complex medical emergencies, while offering an academic upgrading pathway to become SCDF Paramedic Specialists.Just earlier this year, the SCDF and ITE successfully launched the inaugural WSDip in Facilities Management, which attracted over 400 applicants to become Fire and Rescue Section Commanders. The strong response to this programme paves the way for even more work-and-learn opportunities through other WSDip programmes, including the newly launched WSDip in Paramedicine commencing in April 2025 and the upcoming WSDip in Logistics and Supply Chain Management launching in April 2026. caption: [Fire @ 48, Woodlands Drive 16]Earlier today at about 1:25pm, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.The fire, which involved the household shelter and the kitchen of a unit on the 10th floor, was extinguished by firefighters with a water jet. There was no one inside the unit.As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit also sustained heat and smoke damage.About 50 persons from the neighbouring units were evacuated by the police and SCDF as a precautionary measure.A person was assessed by a paramedic for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Woodlands Health Campus. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire was likely caused by an electrical origin in the household shelter.SCDF would like to remind the public to adopt the following good practices to prevent electrical fires:a) Do not overload power sockets with electrical appliances;b) Switch off electrical appliances when not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Frayed wires should be replaced or repaired immediately; d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces; e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at Do not leave batteries or devices to charge unattended for an extended period of time or leave it charging overnight.

caption: [Final Update: Marine Firefighting Operation @ East of Singapore]This morning (21 Oct) at about 10:30am, SCDF was alerted to a fire onboard a vessel anchored in the East Johor Straits.Upon SCDFs arrival, all crew members of the affected vessel had been accounted for and there were no reported injuries. A water monitor from SCDFs Heavy Rescue Vessel was used to conduct defensive firefighting and cool the exterior of the vessel. Once there were no visible signs of fire, marine firefighting specialists boarded the vessel with a water jet to ensure that the fire, which involved the vessels exhaust funnel, had been fully extinguished. Damping down operations* are ongoing. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire has been put out. This is to ensure that deep-seated embers are fully extinguished to prevent any rekindling of the fire.

caption: [Off-Duty Nurse commended for saving the life of a cardiac arrest patient; 5 others recognised for fighting a fire]On 26 July 2024 at about 4:15pm, an off-duty nurse from .sg , Ms Wong Wai Ting was at Causeway Point when she saw Mr Subhan lying unconscious on the floor. After assessing that Mr Subhan had no pulse and was not breathing, Ms Wong immediately commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR). With the help of another person, CPR continued until the arrival of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services. Through their swift action in rendering assistance, Mr Subhan is alive today. SCDF would also like to thank the unidentified member of the public who assisted in this incident. We hope the person can reach out to us so that we can accord due recognition for stepping forward to assist in this incident. In a separate fire incident that occured at Blk 870 Woodlands Street 81 on 1 September 2024, upon receiving a notification via the myResponder app, Mr Izz Ziyad Bin Sharel and Mr Amirul Sufyan rushed to the scene, retrieved a fire extinguisher from a nearby Lifesavers Emergency Point and proceeded to fight the fire which involved a skip bin near the block.Mr Ryan Nicholas Santiago, who had seen the fire from his window, teamed with town council worker Mr Md Mizanur Rahman and his supervisor, Mr Rahman Md Arifur who were nearby, to retrieve the hosereel. Together, the five courageous men helped to contain the fire before SCDF's arrival.On 25 September 2024, the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award was presented to Ms Wong. The SCDF Community First Responder Award were presented to Mr Rahman, Mr Mizanur Rahman, Mr Amirul and Mr Ryan. The awards were presented by COL Bob Tan, Deputy Commander, 4th SCDF Division. As Mr Izz Ziyad is an SCDF civilian officer from Ang Mo Kio Fire Station, he will be commended separately for rendering assistance beyond the call of duty. caption: [Ferry Rescue Exercise (FEREX) 2024] Yesterday (22 Aug), SCDF participated in the FEREX 2024, an annual exercise organised by Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore as part of Singapore Safety Week. The exercise involved over 200 personnel from eight government agencies and industry partners. The multi-agency exercise simulated the collision of two ferries, resulting in a fire onboard one of the ferries and the other ferry at risk of sinking. As part of the exercise, a Rapid Response Fire Vessel, which can reach a top speed of up to 40 knots with high manoeuvrability, was deployed for firefighting, as well as the search and rescue operation. A Heavy Rescue Vessel was also deployed to evacuate passengers, with emergency medical services personnel onboard to triage and render medical assistance to the casualties. FEREX 2024 was a good opportunity for all participating agencies to validate our operational plans and procedures, and test our multi-agency operational response and coordination during a maritime incident. caption: [Fire @ 2, Kim Seng Walk]Earlier today at about 4:50pm, SCDF firefighters from Central Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, black smoke was emitting from a unit on the 18th floor. caption: [Fire @ Block 313, Hougang Avenue 5]Early this morning at about 12:50am (16 Aug), SCDF firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station and Paya Lebar Fire Station responded to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDFs arrival, the living room of a unit on the second floor was on fire, and one person was reported trapped inside the unit.Firefighters immediately conducted forcible entry through the front door and entered the smoke-logged unit. A team of firefighters found the person in the kitchen and brought the person out to safety. The fire was extinguished with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the entire living room was damaged and the rest of the unit sustained heat and soot damage. Four persons were assesed by SCDF paramedics. Two were sent to Singapore General Hospital and one was sent to Changi General Hospital. One person declined to be sent to hospital. About 30 people from the neighbouring units were evacuated by the police as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely started from a Personal Mobility Device (PMD) that was in the living room. The cause of the fire is still under investigation. SCDF would like to remind the public not to charge the batteries for an extended period of time or leave them charging overnight. In addition, do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

caption: [Fire @ Block 612, Ang Mo Kio Avenue 4]Earlier this morning at 1:55am, SCDF was alerted to the fire at the abovementioned location.Firefighters from Ang Mo Kio Fire Station, supported by Bishan Fire Station, entered the smoke-filled unit on the 11th floor to fight the fire. The fire, which involved a bedroom, was extinguished with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and soot damage. 5 persons from the affected unit had evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival. SCDF conveyed two persons to Singapore General Hospital and two persons to KK Womens and Childrens Hospital for smoke inhalation. Another person declined to be sent to hospital. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and soot damages. About 10 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. caption: [29th Rota Commander Course Commissioning Parade] Yesterday (2 Jul), 47 Officer Cadets from the 29th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers in a ceremonial parade held at the Civil Defence Academy. COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF, graced the event as the Event Officiating Officer. The RCC Commissioning Parade is a significant milestone for these graduating cadets, who have undergone a comprehensive training programme to develop their knowledge and skills in firefighting, rescue, and emergency medical response over the course of seven months. As Senior Officers, their tasks include leading their fellow officers in SCDFs lifesaving mission of protecting and saving lives and property. Amongst the graduating cadets were nine Officer Cadets from the Direct-Entry Paramedic Senior Officer scheme. Before joining the 29th RCC, these nine Officer Cadets attended a 12-month Diploma programme in Paramedicine Science at Nanyang Polytechnic, and a 3-month operational attachment at the fire stations. This scheme underscores the transformation of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services (EMS) to meet increasing operational demands while further elevating the service delivery of our EMS to the public. Speaking to the graduating cadets, COMR Eric Yap underlined the importance of the training and development of SCDF officers, guided by SCDFs training philosophy - Train as we would operate; Learn as we innovate. COMR Eric Yap also expressed his appreciation to the families and loved ones of the cadets for their support and encouragement throughout the course.Congratulations to the 29th RCC! We wish them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their journey with the Life Saving Force

The RCC Commissioning Parade is a significant milestone for these graduating cadets, who have undergone a comprehensive training programme to develop their knowledge and skills in firefighting, rescue, and emergency medical response over the course of seven months. As Senior Officers, their tasks include leading their fellow officers in SCDF's lifesaving mission of protecting and saving lives and property. Amongst the graduating cadets were nine Officer Cadets from the Direct-Entry Paramedic Senior Officer scheme. Before joining the 29th RCC, these nine Officer Cadets attended a 12-month Diploma programme in Paramedicine Science at Nanyang Polytechnic, and a 3-month operational attachment at the fire stations. This scheme underscores the transformation of SCDF's Emergency Medical Services (EMS) to meet increasing operational demands while further elevating the service delivery of our EMS to the public. Speaking to the graduating cadets, the Commissioner of SCDF underlined the importance of the training and development of SCDF officers, guided by SCDF's training philosophy - Train as we would operate; Learn as we innovate. The Commissioner of SCDF also expressed his appreciation to the families and loved ones of the cadets for their support and encouragement throughout the course. Congratulations to the 29th RCC! We wish them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their journey with the Life Saving Force.

caption: [Prioritising SCDFs Emergency Medical Services Resources for Life-threatening Emergencies] Demand for SCDFs Emergency Medical Services (EMS) has significantly increased over the years and is expected to continue to trend upwards due to the increasing and ageing population. With this rising demand for SCDFs EMS, SCDF has been prioritising the deployment of our emergency medical resources and response based on the severity of the medical emergency through the SCDFs EMS Tiered Response Framework. First introduced in 2017, various initiatives under the EMS Tiered Response Framework were progressively implemented over the years enhanced medical call triaging by 995 call-takers at SCDF Operations Centre using the advanced medical protocol system, non-conveyance policy and non-dispatch policy for emergency ambulances. These initiatives allow SCDF to manage and prioritise our stretched EMS resources for life-threatening medical emergencies that require more immediate medical attention, and where every second matters. We would like to thank the public for their understanding and support over the years. SCDF remains committed to meet the increasing EMS demand whilst ensuring operational excellence. At the upcoming SCDF Workplan Seminar on 4 July, SCDF will announce two new EMS initiatives which will build on the existing initiatives rolled out under the EMS Tiered Response Framework and continue to prioritise our response for life-threatening medical emergencies. Stay tuned and remember Call995OnlyForEmergencies

caption: [40th Anniversary of the 995 Emergency Number]On 1 July 1984, 995 was established as Singapores fire and ambulance emergency number. At the time, all 995 calls would go to the control room located at Central Fire Station. Today, all 995 calls are handled by the Operations Centre located at SCDFs headquarters at 91, Ubi Avenue 4. The Operations Centre has evolved over the decades, harnessing technology to increase its efficiency. One such technology is the Advanced Command, Control and Communications (C3) Emergency System, which enables SCDF to dispatch emergency vehicles with the fastest arrival time to fire, rescue, or emergency medical incidents, based on live traffic conditions. The system also allows for real-time monitoring on the location of the fleet of emergency vehicles to enhance deployment efficiency. In 2023, the Emergency Video System (EVS) was launched in collaboration with the Singapore Police Force, Home Team Science and Technology Agency, and ST Engineering, enabling 995 callers to transmit live footage of an incident to the Operations Centre. The EVS enhances the Operations Centres situational awareness of the incidents, and also helps to facilitate the decision-making of emergency responders when responding to these incidents. Today, as we commemorate the 40th anniversary of the 995 emergency number, we also salute the Operations Centre Specialists and emergency responders who remain steadfast in our mission to protect and save lives for a safe and secure nation. TheLifeSavingForce

caption: [Thomson-East Coast Line Stage 4 (TEL4) Opening Ceremony: Civil Defence Shelter at Siglap MRT Station]Earlier today, Prime Minister and Minister for Finance attended the TEL4 opening ceremony as the Guest-of-Honour. As part of the ceremony, PM Wong was briefed on the Civil Defence (CD) Shelters, and SCDFs community engagement efforts to promote lifesaving skills such as applying Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), using an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) and Improvised First Aid Skills.CD Public Shelters are prepared, converted, and managed by Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNSmen) from the SCDFs Public Shelter and Resilience Units (PSRUs). caption: [Community First Responders saved the lives of two people who suffered a cardiac arrest] On 17 Feb 2024 at about 9:10pm, Mr Kenneth Wong Kuo Fong was visiting Ms Joanne Hoo Yuen Yuen at her home when Ms Joannes mother, Mdm Ng Lian Koon collapsed. Quickly determining that she was in cardiac arrest, Mr Kenneth asked the visitors in the household to call 995 and he immediately performed Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) with Ms Hoos assistance. Mr Chia Jun Wei , Mr Keefe Tan Yu En and Mr Lokesh Prasad Chinna Chandragari responded upon receiving a notification on the myResponder app. Working as a team, they continued CPR and used an Automated External Defibrillator (AED), which was retrieved from a Lifesavers Emergency Point* at the lift lobby of a nearby block. In another incident on 16 Mar 2024 at about 4:30pm, Mr Law Ghee Beng collapsed from a cardiac arrest at Sengkang Swimming Complex. Springing into action, Senior Lifeguard Donguines Larni Olandesca, Lifeguard Zhu Zhou and Lifeguard Mi Qiang rushed to assist Mr Law. They performed CPR and used an AED. Mr Law subsequently regained consciousness before SCDFs arrival. Thanks to their timely lifesaving actions, both Mdm Ng and Mr Law are alive today. In recognition of their public spiritedness, these Community First Responders were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award on 26 Apr 2024. The awards were presented by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander, 3rd SCDF Division. The presentation was graced by the attendance of the two cardiac arrest survivors who gave their heartfelt thanks to their lifesavers. You too can make a difference. Learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's Responders Plus Programme or attend its online programme at go.gov.sg/scdfrpp *The Lifesavers' Emergency Point is an initiative by the Singapore Civil Defence Force, Temasek Foundation, Housing & Development Board and Town Councils to progressively install fire extinguishers at the lift lobbies of every one in two HDB blocks. These fire extinguishers will be placed together with AEDs that are already installed at the HDB blocks.

caption: [SCDF Day - 35 Years of Protecting and Saving Lives and Property for a Safe and Secure Singapore]On 15 April 1989, the Singapore Fire Service and Singapore Civil Defence Force merged as one, consolidating Singapores fire, rescue and emergency medical services response into a single organisation.To commemorate the merger, the SCDF Day Dining-In ceremony was held at the Civil Defence Academy yesterday evening. This annual ceremony serves as a platform for our officers to rededicate their commitment to our lifesaving mission and reaffirm our core values of Pride and Care. The event was attended by SCDF regular officers, full-time National Servicemen, Operationally Ready National Servicemen and civilian staff.The SCDF Day Dining-In Ceremony was graced by Mrs Josephine Teo, Minister for Communications and Information and Second Minister for Home Affairs. In her speech, Minister Josephine Teo acknowledged and commended SCDF personnel who exemplified SCDFs core values in and beyond the course of their duties. Congratulations to all award winners and wishing all SCDF officers a Happy SCDF Day!

caption: [Community First Responders Commended for Saving Lives] On 18 Feb 2024 at about 1:45am, Mr Chua Fu Shun and Mr Chua Fu Qin were about to head home after visiting their mother when they saw a fire at Block 287A Jurong East Street 21. Without hesitation, the Chua brothers called 995 and rushed to the affected unit on the 8th floor. They quickly called out to the occupants from the affected unit to evacuate. The two brothers also alerted other neighbouring units of the fire. Fortunately, the occupants evacuated in the nick of time and there were no reported injuries. On 24 Feb 2024 at about 8:10am, Assistant Station Manager (ASM) Grace Lim Yen Ling noticed a crowd gathering outside Woodlands MRT station. ASM Grace soon realised that a man had collapsed. ASM Grace immediately called 995 and alerted her colleagues for assistance. Senior Station Manager (SSM) Steven Lim Lin Keat quickly retrieved an Automated External Defibrillator (AED). When ASM Abdul Hadi Bin Ngadino arrived at the scene, he assessed that the collapsed man had no pulse and showed no sign of breathing; ASM Hadi promptly commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR). SSM Andrew Chua Joo Chai, who was off-duty from his night shift, took turns with ASM Hadi to perform CPR. The man was resuscitated before the arrival of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services. On 28 March 2024, these Community First Responders were awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The award was presented by AC Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division. The presentation was graced by Senior Parliamentary Secretary Mdm Rahayu Mahzam, Advisor to Jurong GRC GROs (Bukit Batok East). You too can make a difference. caption: [Electrificationof SCDF Emergency Vehicles]We are excited to witness the launch of Singapore's first electric emergency vehicle at the Milipol Asia-Pacific - Tech X Summit (MAP-TXS) earlier today! caption: [Rubbish Bin Fire Extinguished by a Family of Community First Responders]On 11 Feb 2024 at about 8:55pm, Mr Aeson Chua and his family saw a rubbish bin on fire at Block 932B, Hougang Avenue 9. The fire was threatening to spread to another bin nearby. Springing into action, Mr Aeson accessed a hosereel from a nearby void deck, and fought the fire. His brave young children, Anduin (age 7) and Arwen (age 11) assisted him to uncoil the hosereel drum while he pulled the hosereel towards the fire. His wife, Mdm Sinithra alerted 995 and looked out for the safety of her family. Thanks to their courageous act, the fire was extinguished. SCDF would also like to thank the other members of public who assisted in this incident. We hope they will reach out to us so that we can recognise them as well for their public spiritedness.On 22 March 2024, Mr Aeson and his family were presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award. The award was presented by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander, 3rd SCDF Division.You too can make a difference. The event was graced by Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, who visited Tan Kah Kee MRT Station. caption: [SCDF Annual Statistics 2023]The SCDF annual statistics for Emergency Medical Services (EMS), Fire Incidents, and Fire Safety Enforcement Checks for Year 2023 were released today.Key takeaways:1 SCDF responded to 246,832 EMS calls in 2023, a decrease of 3.9% from 2022. However, the overall EMS demand remained high, with an average of 676 EMS calls daily, which was 30% higher than in 2019 (pre-pandemic). 2 The total number of fire calls increased by 8.6% to 1,954 cases in 2023. 3 There were 970 fires in residential buildings in 2023, an increase of 3.7% from 2022.Fires due to unattended cooking and electrical origin remained the top two causes of fires in residential buildings in 2023. 4 While non-residential fires decreased by 6.9% in 2023, the number of fires in non-building premises rose by 34.9% to 580 cases. These fires in non-building premises included vegetation fires, vehicle fires, as well as fires involving discarded items.5 SCDF stepped up the number of fire safety enforcement checks in 2023. A total of 15,044 fire safety enforcement checks were conducted, an increase of 17.6% from 12,792 in 2022.Read more at

caption: Earlier today, we recognised the efforts of seven remarkable staff of (MBS), for their public-spiritedness in responding to a medical emergency at their hotel. When a guest was found to be suffering from a cardiac arrest during his stay at the hotel, seven staff from MBS security team immediately sprung into action and coordinated their response to the emergency by carrying out the following actions: applying Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on the guest, facilitating lift access and escorting the ambulance crew to the hotel room. These actions not only played a crucial role in expediting our ambulance crews response, but is essential to better the chances of survival, especially in cardiac arrest situation. In recognition of their public-spirited acts, the seven staff were awarded the Community Lifesaver Award at Marina Bay Sands. The awards were presented by COL Mohamed Firoz Bin Ramjan, Commander, 1st SCDF Division. Their swift response during the medical emergency exemplifies strong teamwork and also the importance of equipping ourselves with livesaving skills, such as CPR.CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesavers ANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRoleSGSecure

caption: [Fire @ 287A, Jurong East Street 21] On 18 February 2024 at about 1:50am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. The fire was raging inside a unit on the 8th floor when firefighters from Clementi, Bukit Batok and Jurong Fire Station arrived. The fire, which involved the living room, was extinguished with two water jets.Two persons self-evacuated from the affected unit before SCDF arrived. A person from a neighbouring unit was assessed for smoke inhalation and conveyed to Singapore General Hospital.The cause of the fire is under investigation.Common causes of household fires include unattended cooking, fires caused by electrical origin, and lighted materials like candlelight and burning incense that are left unattended. More information on fire prevention (pg 24-25) is available in the Civil Defence Emergency Handbook, which can be downloaded from the SCDF website.

caption: [28th Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Parade]Earlier today, 44 cadets graduated from the 28th Rota Commander Course (RCC) at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA). Amongst the graduating cohort were two trainees from the General Directorate of Civil Defence, Kingdom of Bahrain, and three trainees from the Brunei Fire and Rescue Department. Over the course of seven months, these cadets have undergone a comprehensive training programme to acquire skills and knowledge in firefighting, rescue and hazardous materials mitigation operations. In his speech, the guest of honour, Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, shared about the second phase of CDAs redevelopment effort, which was completed in July last year. Four new training facilities have been operationalised, which provide RCC cadets with enhanced firefighting and rescue training through realistic simulations using advanced technology. MOS Faishal also spoke about strengthening of community partnerships, emphasising the importance of communitys role as first responders, and highlighted the opening of the Lifesavers Connect Zone at Joo Seng Fire Post in September last year as a significant milestone in SCDFs efforts to enhance community engagement. Congratulations to the 28th RCC! We look forward to your contributions in the Life Saving Force

caption: [Three Community First Responders commended for saving a life] On the afternoon of 17 September 2023, Dr Vianne Lau, a doctor with , was playing badminton at Heartbeat ActiveSG Sport Hall when she saw a man collapsed nearby. Mr Chow Wei Jun, a Guest Officer from who was in the vicinity, also sprang into action and joined Dr Lau in administering CPR. Lifeguard, Mr Lionel Lo Chee Voon, was also alerted of the incident. He promptly retrieved an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) and medical equipment. The trio used the AED to deliver a shock to the man and the man regained consciousness before the arrival of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services. Thanks to their timely lifesaving actions, the man is alive. Kudos to Dr Lau, Mr Chow and Mr Lo! You too can help someone in distress by downloading SCDFs myResponder app and registering as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as cardiac arrest incidents or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. cleaned_caption: [Surge in 995 EMS Calls] 995 Emergency Medical Services (EMS) calls to SCDF have surged to a high of nearly 750 calls a day on average in the first week of December. This is about 100 cases more than the average daily EMS calls between July to September 2023 (Note: Average daily number of EMS calls pre-COVID was about 550). And do you know that almost 5% of medical calls to the 995 hotline are non-emergencies? If EMS calls continue to climb, the public may experience delays in ambulance response, particularly for less critical medical incidents as the SCDF needs to continue prioritising our limited resources for life-threatening medical emergencies. We are monitoring the situation closely. Measures have also been put in place to manage the increase in EMS Calls, some of which are: Redeploying ambulances to areas with higher rates of medical emergency calls, assessing 995 emergency calls and dispatching ambulances only for emergencies, and not conveying to hospital patients who have been assessed by SCDF paramedics to have non-emergency medical conditions. Our 995 call takers, paramedics, and frontliners are doing their best to provide swift conveyance to hospital for people with life-threatening and emergency medical conditions. Here's what YOU can do to help. Refrain from calling 995 if you are not suffering any life-threatening or emergency medical condition. Visit a nearby clinic to seek medical advice instead. Doing so will allow the SCDF to continue providing swift response and conveyance to those who require our emergency medical services the most. See picture for examples of critical, life-threatening medical emergencies.

caption: [13 Persons in the Marine Community Commended for their Public-Spirited Acts during Emergencies at Sea] On 13 September 2023 at about 4:30pm, Mr Ahmad Bonda, a yacht crew member, was out at sea off Lazarus Island when he noticed an unconscious person floating face down. Mr Ahmad Bonda immediately paddled out and brought the person to shore with the help of his friends, Ms Flora Lee, Mr Jay Leong and Mr Benjamin Leong. Upon reaching the shore, Mr Ahmad Bonda promptly commenced cardiopulmonary resuscitation on the person. Three members of the public, Mr Wayne Liew, Mr Bruce Ong and Mr Mithu Muhammad Saminul Alam, who were in the vicinity, also quickly stepped forward to render assistance and ferried the person to St Johns jetty, where he was evacuated to Marina South Pier by SCDF. As a result of their prompt and coordinated lifesaving actions, the person survived and is alive today. In a separate incident on 4 September 2023 at about 1pm, a vessel off Seraya Buoy, located off the south-western coast of Singapore, caught fire. Two tugboats with six crew members onboard responded to the call for assistance. The crew on the first tugboat, Mr Daning Setiawan, Mr Syafei and Mr Dedi Masluhi, conducted the firefighting operation, while Mr Harimurti Raharjo, Mr Abdul Kadir and Mr Rahman were on standby on the second tugboat to provide additional support if required. For their civic-minded actions, the 13 Good Samaritans were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award and the SCDF Community First Responder Award. The awards were presented by COL Ryan Ong, Commander of SCDFs Marine Division, and SUPT Desmond Ong, Commanding Officer, Brani Region, 's Police Coast Guard, on 29 November 2023. The presentation was also attended by Capt. Chong Jia Chyuan, Senior Deputy Director (Operations), Port Master, . You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as cardiac arrest incidents or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity.

caption: [Graduation Ceremony for the Inaugural CDAU Emergency Medical Technician Course] Yesterday afternoon (11 Oct), 12 Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit (CDAU) officers graduated from the inaugural CDAU Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) Course.These newly minted CDAU officers will perform frontline duties at the fire stations by responding to medical emergencies as an EMT alongside the paramedic in an ambulance. Apart from emergency medical services, CDAU officers serve an important role in complementing SCDF regular and full-time National Servicemen (NSF) in vocations such as Firefighting and Rescue, Public Education, Enforcement and Heritage Gallery Guides. The CDAU EMT course was conducted during weekday evenings and weekends over a period of about 20 weeks at the SCDFs National EMS Training Centre (NETC). CDAU officers undergo the same training syllabus and assessments that SCDF regular officers and NSFs go through. The graduation ceremony was officiated by SAC Abdul Razak, Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department. I am very proud of the inaugural batch of CDAU officers who have qualified as Emergency Medical Technicians. Their commitment to the spirit of volunteerism by undergoing this advanced pre-hospital care training reflects that Singapore is well on its way to become a Nation of Lifesavers. I hope these officers will inspire others to step forward and upskill themselves in the lifesaving mission. - SAC Abdul Razak. Find out more about how to be a CDAU officer and volunteer to save lives in the Home Team Volunteer Network website at . About 80 SCDF officers and 20 emergency vehicles were deployed for the incident. At the height of the firefighting operation, firefighters used two water jets to fight the fire from inside the building, and two aerial water monitors were deployed to contain the fire from the exterior of the building.The fire, which involved furniture and alcohol products within the two workshop units, was extinguished by SCDF at 10pm. caption: [Five Persons Commended for Sea Rescue at Sentosa]On the morning of 9 July 2023, a group of six persons were using a kayak in the waters off Tanjong Beach, Sentosa when strong currents capsized their kayak. They managed to rescue four of the kayakers.Mr Ahmad Hamim Bin Mohammad Hanib and Mr Jasmil Bin Jaafar who were working at the Ola Beach club nearby also responded to help using jet skis and rescued the last two kayakers. caption: [IBM Think Singapore 2023]The IBM Think Singapore was held on 14 Sep, which saw the launch of a first-of-its-kind 5G Artificial Intelligence (AI) project that will enhance the operational readiness of SCDF frontliners.Underpinned by 5G technology, the project features AI headsets coupled with visual recognition technologies to automate the inspection and monitor the inventory of equipment, as well as Augmented Reality (AR) to give SCDF ground commanders enhanced realism and live access to fire investigation specialists during post-fire investigations. caption: [Community First Responder Commended for Saving a Life] On the morning of 16 Jul 2023, Mr Patrick Cheong was driving to work when he received an alert on the myResponder app notifying him of a case of cardiac arrest at Block 10, Chai Chee Road. Without hesitation, he acknowledged the alert and responded to the location. Upon arrival, he found a lady suffering from cardiac arrest inside a residential unit and her husband was performing Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on her. Mr Patrick immediately rendered assistance to the lady by using an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) that he had retrieved from a nearby block. Three shocks were administered to the patient using the AED. Mr Patrick and the patient's husband continued CPR until the arrival of SCDF's Emergency Medical Services.Thanks to Mr Patrick's lifesaving actions, the patient survived and is alive today. Today (8 Sep), Mr Patrick was presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The award was presented by COL Chew Keng Tok, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division. The patient attended the presentation and expressed her gratitude to Mr Patrick in person. As SCDF commemorates World First Aid Day tomorrow (9 Sep), Mr Patrick's actions serves as a stellar example that anyone can help to save a life and demonstrate the importance of first aid in a medical emergency. "Thanks to your help, I woke up. I recognised all my loved ones. I can walk, talk, sing, read, write and play with my daughter. My husband and I are so grateful to you. There are no words to describe it. You could have ignored the myResponder app alert, been too scared or not wanted the drama on a Sunday morning. Instead, you responded and became a hero." - Quote from cardiac arrest survivor to Mr Patrick. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. caption: [Official Opening of Joo Seng Fire Post with Lifesavers Connect Zone] The Joo Seng Fire Post (JSFP) with the first Lifesavers Connect Zone (LCZ) co-located with it, was officially opened today (5 Sep) by Assoc Prof Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. Located at Blk 9 Joo Seng Road, the JSFP provides emergency response to fire, rescue and emergency medical incidents around the Macpherson-Woodleigh area. SCDF now has a network of 23 fire stations and 28 fire posts providing islandwide emergency services coverage. At the LCZ which features interactive kiosks, members of the public can engage in self-directed learning or hands-on practice on lifesaving skills. These skills include Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Improvised First Aid Skills, and In-Place Protection procedures. In our vision to build ANationOfLifesavers, SCDF will continue to deepen public engagement and increase touch-points in the heartlands for our community to learn emergency preparedness skills by co-locating more LCZs with fire posts in the near future.

caption: [ASEAN Disaster Management Week]The inaugural ASEAN Disaster Management Week (ADMW) 2023 is a week-long event held from 21 to 24 August 2023 with activities of the ASEAN Committee on Disaster Management (ACDM). Themed Disaster Resilience in ASEAN Now and Beyond, the ADMW 2023 serves as a platform to commemorate the achievements of ASEAN in disaster management and disaster risk reduction efforts, and charts ASEANs progress and strategies in disaster resilience. Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, graced the official opening of the ADMW 2023 as the Guest-of-Honour earlier today (22 Aug). Also in attendance was Her Excellency Iwona Pirko, European Union Ambassador to Singapore. In his opening remarks, Minister Shanmugam reaffirmed the importance of the cooperation and coordination among ASEAN Member States to further strengthen our resilience and collective response to disasters in the ASEAN region and beyond. The ADMW 2023 is co-organised by SCDF, the National Focal Point for the ACDM Singapore, the ASEAN Secretariat, the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (), European Union, Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, Asian Development Bank, and Temasek Foundation. Around 200 guests including Ambassadors, and representatives from the ACDM, ASEANs Partners, United Nations, as well as the private sector and non-governmental organisations, will be attending the key events during the ADMW in Singapore.

caption: [Fire @ Blk 71, Redhill Road]At about 7:20am today, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon arrival, SCDF firefighters were alerted by residents that there were occupants trapped inside the smoke-logged unit on the 7th floor. SCDF firefighters from Alexandra Fire Station and Marina Bay Fire Station immediately conducted forcible entry into the unit by breaking the padlock of the metal gate.The fire was located at the corner of the living room and was extinguished by SCDF with several buckets of water. While the fire was being extinguished, another team of firefighters that were searching the premises found three children inside the toilet at the back of the kitchen. The children were carried out from the unit by the firefighters and assessed by an ambulance crew. All three children were conveyed to KK Women's and Children's Hospital for smoke inhalation. Before SCDFs arrival, two persons from the affected unit managed to evacuate through a bedroom window. They were assessed for smoke inhalation but declined to be sent to the hospital. In the midst of SCDF's operation, five cats were also brought out of the affected unit.About 25 persons from neighbouring units were evacuated by the SCDF and Police as a precautionary measure.Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from the batteries of two personal mobility devices (PMD) that were charging in the living room.SCDF would like to remind the public on the prevention of PMD/PAB fires, including not to charge batteries for an extended period of time or overnight. Do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

caption: [Cardiac Arrest Patient Saved by Three Community First Responders] On 3 June 2023, Mr Nabil Bin Juraimi was at VivoCity Shopping Mall with his wife, Ms Nur Syafiqah Binte Mazlan and his brother, Mr Nafis Bin Juraimi, when they encountered a person who had collapsed at the basement (B2) of the mall. The trio immediately sprung into action to render aid to the collapsed person. Working as a team, they performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation, and used an automated external defibrillator on the person. Upon SCDF's arrival, they also assisted to direct the ambulance crew to the collapsed person. Mr Nabil and Ms Nur Syafiqah are nurses from Ng Teng Fong General Hospital, while Mr Nafis is an SCDF Operationally Ready National Serviceman. As a result of their timely lifesaving actions, the patient is alive today. Kudos to Mr Nabil, Ms Nur Syafiqah and Mr Nafis. On 26 July 2023, Mr Nabil, Ms Nur Syafiqah and Mr Nafis were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by Colonel Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department. You too can help by downloading SCDFs myResponder app and register as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. caption: [Two Community First Responders commended for saving a life] On 11 June 2023 at about 10:00pm, Mr Lim Kim Thia and Mr Lum Guang Ye were in their own homes when they received an alert on the myResponder app for a cardiac arrest incident at Block 259 Bukit Batok East Avenue 4. Both Community First Responders (CFRs) sprang into action and rushed to the abovementioned location. Mr Lim was the first to arrive at the scene and commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) after assessing that the patient had no pulse and was not breathing. Mr Lum retrieved an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) from the void deck of a nearby block and arrived soon after Mr Lim. Mr Lum prepared the AED while Mr Lim continued CPR. The CFRs then used the AED to deliver a shock to the patient before the arrival of an SCDF ambulance. As a result of their prompt and timely lifesaving actions, the patient is alive today. Kudos to Mr Lim and Mr Lum! On 4 July 2023, the two CFRs were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by Lieutenant Colonel Khaisarah Mansor, Head Community Engagement, 4th SCDF Division. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a CFR via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. caption: [Road Traffic Accident along SLE]On 2 August 2023 at about 3:20pm, SCDF was alerted to a road traffic accident involving a lorry and a truck along the SLE towards BKE, before the Lentor Avenue exit. Upon SCDF's arrival, a man was found trapped in the driver's seat of the lorry. As the front of the lorry was severely crushed inwards, the man's lower limbs were pinned under the dashboard. An SCDF ambulance crew rendered medical aid to stabilise the man's injuries while rescuers, including officers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), conducted the rescue operation. To rescue the man, SCDF rescuers used two hydraulic extendable ramps to exert force on the dashboard, pushing it away from him and creating sufficient space to free his lower limbs. Cutting equipment was also used by rescuers to carefully remove the clutch pedal that had trapped the man's left foot.The man was rescued and conveyed to Khoo Teck Puat Hospital.

caption: [Elevating Training, Learning and Development - SCDF's Workplan Seminar 2023]SCDF's Workplan Seminar (WPS) 2023 was held yesterday (31 Jul), where more than 300 guests were in attendance at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA). Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law graced the event as our Guest-of-Honour. Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development was also present at the WPS, along with representatives from international fire departments. In line with this year's WPS theme of "Elevating Training, Learning and Development", the seminar showcased how we will be preparing our officers for future challenges through our redeveloped Field Training Area (FTA). One of the centrepiece of the FTAs is the National Emergency Medical Services Training Centre, which is built to replicate the real-world pre-hospital emergency care environment. This helps our EMS responders train for diverse emergencies from onsite medical intervention to end-to-end clinical care. The redeveloped FTA also comprises the Fire Research Centre, which is a purpose-built environment for burn testing and enhanced fire modelling capability to aid SCDF in developing improved firefighting techniques. These are two of the seven purpose-built facilities at CDA that will offer enhanced learning and training realism for emergency responders.The third and final phase of CDA's redevelopment will entail the refitting of new fire simulators in our nine-storey furnace building. Phase three is targeted to be ready by next year. SCDFworkplan2023
