caption: [Fire @ Blk 618 Bedok Reservoir Road] Early this morning (21 July) at about 3:40am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, black smoke was seen emitting from a unit on the 7th floor. Donned with breathing apparatuses, firefighters quickly entered the smoke-logged unit to fight the fire. The fire, which involved a bedroom and part of the living room, was extinguished by SCDF with a water jet. Due to the intense heat of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and smoke damage. Two persons had evacuated the affected unit before SCDF's arrival. Both were assessed by an SCDF paramedic for smoke inhalation. One of them was conveyed to the Singapore General Hospital and the other declined to be sent to the hospital. About 90 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire was caused by an electrical origin in the affected bedroom.*Fire Safety Tips:*SCDF would like to remind the public on some good practices to adopt in the household to prevent electrical fires from occurring:a) Never overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off electrical appliances when not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Wires that are frayed or cracked should be replaced or repaired immediately;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces;e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at ; f) Do not leave batteries or devices charging unattended for an extended period of time or overnight.

caption: [Marine Firefighting Operation @ Southeast of Singapore]Last night (11 July) at about 9:35 p.m., SCDF was alerted to a fire on a vessel anchored off the southeast of Singapore, near Tanah Merah Ferry Terminal.A total of four SCDF marine firefighting and rescue vessels and about 40 marine firefighting specialists from Brani and West Coast Marine Fire Stations were deployed to the incident. Arriving alongside the anchored vessel, the marine firefighting specialists boarded the vessel and using a water jet, they extinguished the fire which was confined to two accommodation decks.Before SCDF's arrival, the vessel's crew had set up three water jets to cool the exterior of the vessel and two water jets to control the fire. Cooling of the vessel's exterior is known as boundary cooling, this helps to reduce the temperature of the vessel's metal structure.After the fire was extinguished, the damping down* operation continued until about 5:00 a.m. today.There were no reported injuries and all crew members of the affected vessel were accounted for. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent the potential rekindling of the fire.

caption: [27th Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Parade]Yesterday, 48 Officer Cadets from the 27th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy. Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, Deputy Chairperson, Government Parliamentary Committee (Home Affairs & Law), graced the event as the Guest-of-Honour.The RCC commissioning ceremony is a significant milestone that marks the transition of Officer Cadets into Senior Officers after a 28-week residential course. During the course, the Officer Cadets, comprising both Regular Officers, Full-time National Servicemen as well as international trainees hailing from Bahrain and Vietnam, were equipped with the requisite operational skills and knowledge to perform the role of frontline commanders.The 27th RCC is also the first batch of Officer Cadets to include nine Direct-Entry Paramedic Senior Officers. Prior to joining the 27th RCC, the nine Paramedic Officer Cadets went through a 12-month paramedicine training course at Nanyang Polytechnic and a three month operational attachment at the frontline fire stations. The SCDF Paramedic Senior Officer scheme underscores the transformation of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services (EMS) to meet increasing operational demands while further elevating the service delivery of our EMS to the public.In speaking to the graduating cadets, Mr Zhulkarnain emphasised the importance of leadership, responsibility and upholding high operational standards while carrying out their respective lifesaving roles and responsibilities. He also underlined the need to uphold the hard-earned public trust which generations of SCDF officers have worked hard to nurture, through professionalism, commitment, and dedication to serving the public.Congratulations to the 27th RCC! We look forward to their contributions in the Life Saving Force Pic 1,3: CPL Gao Wei Jie, Civil Defence Academy Pic 2,4-10: CPL Goh Rhy Yan, Civil Defence Academy

caption: [Fire @ Block 308 Hougang Ave 5]Earlier this evening at about 7:30p.m., SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location.Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was raging in a bedroom of a 13th-floor unit. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit also sustained heat and soot damage.An occupant from the affected unit had evacuated prior to SCDF's arrival.As a precautionary measure, about 10 residents from neighbouring units were evacuated by the police.An SCDF paramedic assessed a person from the affected unit for smoke inhalation but the person declined to be conveyed to the hospital. caption: [Four Nurses Presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award] On 4 February 2023, two off-duty nurses from , Ms Suraidah Binte Selamat and Ms Norazlin Binte Dawood were travelling along Sumang Walk when they noticed a group of people attending to a man, Mr Lee Chee Hoe, who was lying unconscious on the ground. The duo suspected that Mr Lee was suffering from a cardiac arrest, and immediately carried out Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on him. Another member of public also assisted to retrieve a nearby AED. Upon receiving the AED, the two nurses administered shocks to Mr Lee using the AED, and continued to administer CPR on him prior to SCDFs arrival. As a result of their prompt actions, Mr Lee Chee Hoe survived. On 17 May 2023, Ms Suraidah and Ms Norazlin were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. I am very fortunate that I have been saved and it is like a second chance at life. I feel really blessed and I would like to give a big thank you to all of you. Mr Lee Chee Hoe, cardiac arrest survivor SCDF understands that there are other members of the public who have helped out during the abovementioned incident. We would greatly appreciate if these lifesavers could reach out to us so that we can also recognise their good deeds. In another incident on 3 March 2023, another two off-duty nurses from , Ms Ng Siok Qi and Ms Cherie Koh, rendered medical assistance to a person who felt unwell at Changi Airport Terminal 3. Ms Ng Siok Qi and Ms Cherie Koh were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award by COL Chew Keng Tok, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division on 17 May. caption: [Tampines West Community Resilience Day]Yesterday (21 May), more than400 participantsattended the Tampines West Community Resilience (CR) Day.Held at Tampines West Community Centre, the event was graced by Mr Masagos Zulkifli,Minister for Social and Family Development, Second Minister for Health & Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs, Advisor to Tampines Grassroots Organisations (GROs). Jointly organised by 2nd SCDF Division, National Fire and Emergency Preparedness Council (NFEC), Peoples Association, and the Tampines West Community Emergency and Engagement (C2E) Committee, the CR Day aims to impart members of the public with Emergency Preparedness (EP) knowledge and skills. This includes basic firefighting using a fire extinguisher, Improvised First Aid Skills (IFAS), administering Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), and using an Automated External Defibrillator (AED).During the event, Mr Masagos also presented three members of the public with the Community First Responder Award and five members of the public with the Community Lifesaver Award. Their quick thinking and willingness to step forward and render help to others during an emergency is truly commendable.Don't fret if you have missed this CR Day, members of the public are strongly encouraged to join us at our next CR Day on 28 May 2023, at 175A, Lompang Road. Apart from the CR Day, the public can also learn essential EP knowledge and skills through SCDFs Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP) and register as a Community First Responder (CFR) via SCDFs myResponder app.Register for the CEPP through the link in our bio and join us towards building ANationofLifesavers!

caption: [Fire @ Block 511 West Coast Drive]At about 11:15 p.m. yesterday (20 May), SCDF was alerted to a fire in a 12th floor unit at the abovementioned location.The fire, which involved the contents of a bedroom, was extinguished by firefighters from Clementi Fire Station using a water jet.Six occupants from the affected unit evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival. Do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

caption: [Four Gurkha Contingent Officers Commended for Saving the Life of a Cardiac Arrest Victim] On 25 Mar 2023, at about 11:30 a.m., four officers from Gurkha Contingent (GC) of the were driving in the vicinity of Woodlands Industrial Park, where they saw a man lying motionless by the roadside of Woodlands Industrial Park D Street 1. Team Leader Senior Staff Sergeant (SSS) Man Kumar Limbu and Operator Corporal (CPL) Dinesh Limbu quickly approached the unconscious man and found him in a state of cardiac arrest. SSS Man Kumar immediately called for an ambulance and directed CPL Dinesh and Operator CPL Jeevan Gharti Magar to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on the man. At the same time, Deputy Team Leader Sergeant (SGT) Sabin Gurung managed the oncoming traffic for the safety of the man and the officers rendering CPR. The officers continued with the CPR on the unconscious man until the arrival of an SCDF ambulance. As a result of the prompt and timely lifesaving actions by the GC officers, the man is recovering well today. Yesterday (17 May), the four officers were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by Colonel Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a Community First Responder (CFR) via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted of nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. Being trained in basic firefighting, first aid and CPR is useful but not mandatory to qualify as a CFR! Anyone who is willing can do something to help . Everyone counts; every action matters!Join us as a CFR today by signing up on the myResponder app here: CommunityFirstResponderCommuityLifesaversANationofLivesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesOurResponseMattersWeMakeSGSecure

Goh, a teacher of the late SGT1 Edward H Go, as a moving tribute to her former student.Read more on the story through the link in our bio. [An 8-minute read]

caption: [Memorandum of Understanding between SCDF and SIT]Earlier today (12 May), a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Singapore Civil Defence Force and Singapore Institute of Technology (SIT) was signed. The MoU was signed by Assistant Commissioner (AC) Francis Ng, Director of Training & Professional Development Department, SCDF and Mr Bernard Nee, Deputy President (Industry & Community), SIT.The MoU provides a collaborative framework for SCDF and SIT to pursue research projects and develop training courses in industrial fire safety. The SIT Electrical Safety Symposium held in January 2023 had embarked on the professional exchanges between SCDF and SIT to benefit the larger community of practice that pursues industrial fire safety.AC Francis Ng, Director of Training & Professional Development Department, SCDF, shared that building strategic partnerships with valued partners remains one of SCDFs top priorities. "The signing of this MoU represents our commitment to growth, progress and excellence, and provides a collaborative framework to leverage our unique strengths, expertise, and resources to achieve shared goals.The SCDFs Fire Research Centre located in the Civil Defence Academy would be commissioned in mid-2023 to provide a state-of-the-art facility for research and development for fire science and fire safety. The MoU will facilitate mutual benefitting projects to enhance the knowledge capacity of both organisations and elevate overall industrial fire safety standards in Singapore.

caption: [Unveiling of Memorial Garden at Civil Defence Heritage Gallery]An outdoor Memorial Garden paying tribute to SCDF officers who lost their lives in the line of duty was unveiled at the Civil Defence Heritage Gallery this evening. The Memorial Garden is open to members of the public when they visit the Civil Defence Heritage Gallery.

caption: [SCDF Conferred Medal of Appreciation by the Republic of Trkiye]Earlier this evening, SCDF was conferred the Medal of Appreciation by the Vice President of the Republic of Trkiye, H.E. Fuat Oktay. The Medal of Appreciation is in recognition of SCDFs search and rescue efforts following an earthquake in Trkiye in February 2023. Two days after the devastating earthquake, a 68-member Operation Lionheart Contingent comprising rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), paramedic and medical specialists, search specialists and operation support officers were deployed in two waves. LTC Lok Wee Keong, DART Commander, represented SCDF to receive the award at the Presidency of the Republic of Trkiye in Ankara, Trkiye. "The SCDF is honoured to be conferred with the Medal of Appreciation from the Vice President of the Republic of Trkiye, H.E. Fuat Oktay. The medal recognises the search and rescue efforts by SCDFs Operation Lionheart Contingent that was deployed to Trkiye in February this year as part of Singapores humanitarian assistance and disaster relief efforts. The SCDF values the strong friendship and bonds forged with our Trkiye counterparts during the deployment. The people of Trkiye have demonstrated admirable resilience and fortitude, and we are confident they would emerge much stronger as they rebuild their lives and homes." - Commissioner Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF

caption: [SCDF Day @ The Istana] In commemoration of SCDF Day 2023, a Garden Reception was held earlier this evening at The Istana.Celebrated annually on 15 April, SCDF Day recognises the integration of the Singapore Fire Service and SCDF 34 years ago, and celebrates the significant milestones achieved by SCDF over the years.The SCDF Garden Reception was graced by President Halimah Yacob. Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, together with more than 400 SCDF officers, SCDFs strategic partners and volunteers, and officers from the Minister of Home Affairs, were also present at this momentous event. In his opening address, Minister Shanmugam thanked all SCDF officers for their unwavering dedication to the Life Saving mission. He also reaffirmed the importance of our collective commitment to a safe and secure Singapore, and expressed his confidence in SCDF's operational capabilities. 16 awards were presented by Minister Shanmugam during the Reception to recognise the exemplary performance of SCDF officers who have gone beyond the call of duty and have embodied the SCDFs core values of Pride and Care. These recipients comprised Regulars, Full-time National Servicemen (NSF), and Operationally Ready National Servicemen (NSmen).During the Reception, President Halimah Yacob interacted with some of the award recipients, NSmen, SCDFs strategic partners and volunteers, as well as SCDFs Operation Lionheart contingent which was deployed to Trkiye for disaster relief efforts in February 2023. SCDF has come a long way since its founding years. As we give recognition to our SCDF officers today, we also reaffirm our dedication to our Life Saving mission, and will remain committed to our Transformation journey towards ANationOfLifesavers.PrideandCare OurPeopleOurPride

caption: [Resident Puts Out Kitchen Stove Fire] On 6 Mar 2023, at about 5:15 p.m., Mr Bryan Toh was washing his car at the outdoor carpark of his condominium along Cashew Road when he noticed smoke coming out of a unit on the ground floor. Mr Bryan went to investigate and noticed that the kitchen stove in the unit was on fire. Springing into action, he alerted the neighbouring units to evacuate and called 995. He then rushed back to his car to get his domestic water hose, which he connected to a water tap, about 20 meters away from the affected unit and fought the fire. Mr Bryan successfully extinguished the fire before SCDFs arrival and there were no reported casualties. Kudos to Mr Bryan! On 3 Apr 2023, Mr Bryan was presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award for his prompt and timely actions. The award was presented by COL Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division. You too can help by downloading SCDFs myResponder app and register as a Community First Responder via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or a minor fire that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. caption: [Memorandum of Understanding between DFES and SCDF]Earlier this week, a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was signed between the Department of Fire and Emergency Services (DFES), Western Australia, and SCDF at the Civil Defence Academy.The MOU signing ceremony was witnessed by Hon. Minister Stephen Dawson MLC, Minister for Emergency Services, Western Australia, and Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. This MOU signing marks our continued partnership with DFES, where it was first established in 2005. The MOU aims to facilitate the sharing of information and ideas on the delivery of firefighting and emergency services. It also encourages the exchange of knowledge and expertise on Urban Search and Rescue (USAR), and Chemical, Biological and Radiological (CBR) threats. With this MOU, it also reaffirms our partnership with DFES through the attachment of officers for professional and personal development.We look forward to the close collaboration with DFES as both agencies work towards our shared mission of protecting and saving lives and property! caption: [Exercise Northstar XI @ Jurong Island] Earlier today, Exercise Northstar XI (XNS11) was held at Jurong Island to validate multi-agency emergency response plans and hone coordination among national agencies. More than 300 personnel from SCDF, various key government agencies and industry partners participated in the exercise. The XNS11 began with an armed adversary scenario and a sea interdiction response, where the perpetrators were jointly neutralised by SAFs Island Defence Task Force and SPFs Ground Response Force, Emergency Response Team, and Police Coast Guard. Albeit that the perpetrators were neutralised, improvised explosive devices planted on Jurong Island were detonated remotely causing a chemical pipeline rupture and two oil tank fires. These scenarios were mitigated with the response of SCDF resources, among which were the HazMat Control Vehicle, HazMat Mitigation Vehicle, and SCDFs latest Modular Oil Tank Firefighting System. Mr Lee Hsien Loong, Prime Minister (PM) of Singapore, together with Cabinet members, were present to observe the exercise. In speaking to the media after the exercise, PM Lee reaffirmed the importance of inter-agency response during major emergencies to safeguard Singapores national security. In pursuing our shared mission of a safe and secure Singapore, XNS11 was an enriching opportunity for SCDF to work alongside other agencies to test and validate the Whole-of-Government response framework in the event of major crises and potential threat scenarios. Check out the photos to see what transpired during XNS11!XNS11ANationofLifesavers

caption: [Memorandum of Understanding between BASARNAS and SCDF]Earlier today, a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was signed between the National Search and Rescue Agency (BASARNAS) of Indonesia and SCDF.This MOU was one of several MOUs signed at the Singapore-Indonesia Leaders Retreat held at the Istana, where Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong met Indonesian President Joko Widodo, and reaffirmed the excellent state of relations between Singapore and Indonesia.The signing of the MOU between BASARNAS and SCDF was represented by Air Marshal Henri Alfiandi, Head of the National Search and Rescue Agency, and COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF.Under the MOU, both agencies will explore new areas of collaboration and growth opportunities, including Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) capacity building, exchange of knowledge and expertise in USAR, as well as provision of mutual assistance in the event of a natural disaster.Todays signing marks yet another milestone in the partnership between BASARNAS and SCDF. caption: [Lifesavers on the Move] Since 2015, SCDF has been galvanising the business community from the transport, logistics and courier industries to support and participate in the SCDF AED-on-Wheels programme - an important component of the SCDFs Save-A-Life initiative. Yesterday (13 March), we welcomed our latest partner - SingPost. To date, this programme has a membership of 310 participants, comprising private hire drivers, drivers from the logistics and courier service industry, such as Strides Taxi, Grab, ComfortDelGro and Ninja Van, as well as drivers from the general community. With SingPost joining the programme, there will be more AED equipped vehicles. Providers from the logistics and courier service industry have an extensive presence on our roads and hence they can play a critical life-saving role in our community while plying the roads. The participants under the AED-on-Wheels programme are also registered Community First Responders (CFRs). As CFRs, they are trained in basic firefighting, first aid, cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and the use of AED under the SCDFs Community Emergency Preparedness Programme. When alerted of cardiac arrests cases via the SCDFs myResponder App, drivers in the vicinity can proceed to the scene, perform CPR and administer AED on the cardiac arrest victim thereby improving the chances of survival. SCDF is grateful to the public, stakeholders and partners in supporting our mission of protecting and saving lives and property. We will endeavour to grow and expand the various community partnership programmes, including the AED-on-Wheels programme further! caption: [Final Update: Fire @ 28, Tuas South Avenue 8]At about 6:15 p.m. yesterday (13 March), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the above location. The fire, the size of about one and a half football fields, had engulfed an industrial building consisting of warehouse and production areas, including a six-storey production unit. The fire involved chemical solvents and flammable construction materials. A total of 26 emergency vehicles and about 80 personnel were deployed for this incident. At the height of the firefighting operation, SCDF firefighters deployed eight water jets and an Unmanned Firefighting Machine. The fire was brought under control at about 8:15 p.m. Earlier in the evening, two workers were assessed by an SCDF paramedic for blisters on the hands and forehead respectively. They refused conveyance to the hospital. There were no other reported persons who had sustained injuries. The firefighting operation is still ongoing. Once the fire has been extinguished, firefighters will remain at the site to damp down* the affected areas with water. *Damp down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent the potential rekindling of the fire.

caption: [International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) Team Leaders and Working Groups Meeting 2023]The annual International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) Team Leaders and Working Groups Meeting 2023 was hosted in Singapore this year, from 28 February to 2 March 2023. Co-organised by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) and SCDF, more than 100 participants from 46 countries gathered at the Civil Defence Academy to assess the operational capabilities of international Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) response.The opening remarks were delivered by AC Michael Chua, Director Operations, SCDF, Mr Murat Kozluklu, First Secretary, Embassy of the Republic of Trkiye, and Mr Winston Chang, INSARAG Secretariat Worldwide, Emergency Response Section, OCHA Geneva. In their remarks, they reaffirmed the importance of a coordinated USAR response and expressed their gratitude to the Team Leadersand Working Groupsfor their dedication and commitment to the INSARAG mission. COL Mehmet Baykal from the Embassy of the Republic of Trkiye also graced the event.With the recent Trkiye-Syria earthquake, this year's meeting was particularly significant as it exemplified the importance of USAR response capabilities globally in times of need. Notwithstanding the devastating impact of the earthquake, coordinated efforts from the Team Leadersand Working Groupsenabled the quick deployment of international USAR teams to render assistance to the local communities in Trkiye and Syria.To strengthen the coordination and effectiveness of international USAR response, the INSARAG Team Leadersand Working Groupsparticipated in constructive discussions to evaluate their response in an ever-evolving landscape. They also discussed training matters based on lessons gleaned from previous USAR operations and exercises.We look forward to our continued partnership with the INSARAG network and stand ever ready to contribute to the international search and rescue community when called upon.

In their remarks, they reaffirmed the importance of a coordinated USAR response and expressed their gratitude to the Team Leadersand Working Groupsfor their dedication and commitment to the INSARAG mission. COL Mehmet Baykal from the Embassy of the Republic of Trkiye also graced the event.With the recent Trkiye-Syria earthquake, this year's meeting was particularly significant as it exemplified the importance of USAR response capabilities globally in times of need. Notwithstanding the devastating impact of the earthquake, coordinated efforts from the Team Leadersand Working Groupsenabled the quick deployment of international USAR teams to render assistance to the local communities in Trkiye and Syria.To strengthen the coordination and effectiveness of international USAR response, the INSARAG Team Leadersand Working Groupsparticipated in constructive discussions to evaluate their response in an ever-evolving landscape. They also discussed training matters based on lessons gleaned from previous USAR operations and exercises.We look forward to our continued partnership with the INSARAG network and stand ever ready to contribute to the international search and rescue community when called upon.

caption: [Two members of public commended for putting out fires in the neighbourhood] On 30 Jan 2023 at about 3:30 a.m., Mr Syamil Uwayis Bin Zainal Abas was resting at home when he received an alert through the SCDF myResponder app for a fire at Block 488A Choa Chu Kang Avenue 5. Mr Syamil proceeded to the Block and saw smoke coming out of the centralised rubbish chute at the ground floor. Without hesitation, he called 995 and proceeded to extinguish the fire with a fire extinguisher that was in the centralised rubbish chute room. In a separate incident on 10 Feb 2023 at about 5:20 p.m., Mr Raymond Lim Koon Siang was on his way to fetch his child from school when he saw smoke coming out from a 2nd floor unit at Block 663 Choa Chu Kang Crescent. Instinctively, Mr Raymond dashed to retrieve a fire extinguisher from his truck which was parked nearby, and rushed to the affected unit. He entered the unit and extinguished the fire involving the kitchen stove and cabinet. Yesterday (28 Feb), the two members of public were presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award for their civic-minded actions. The awards were presented by COL Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a Community First Responder via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. caption: [SCDF Volunteers at the Singapore Red Cross Fundraising Pumpathon 2023] Jointly organised by SCDF and the Singapore Red Cross (SRC), a 10-hour long Pumpathon was held at Shaw Centre today to aid disaster victims in the aftermath of the Trkiye-Syria earthquake. From 11 a.m. to 9 p.m, more than 50 SCDF Volunteers from the Civil Defence Lionhearter Club, National Civil Defence Cadet Corps and Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit pumped six water filtration devices for 10 hours continuously to garner public support and raise funds for the earthquake victims in Trkiye and Syria. This event was especially meaningful as it simulated what displaced populations in disaster stricken areas had to go through to obtain access to clean water.Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, and Associate Professor Ho Peng Kee, Chairman/Home Team Volunteer Network, Ministry of Home Affairs, graced the event and showed their support to the volunteers. His Excellency, Mr Mehmet Burin Gnenli, Turkish Ambassador to Singapore, also attended the event and expressed his appreciation to the volunteers for their hard work. Together, we can all make a difference to the earthquake victims in times of need.

caption: [Update 16: SCDF's Operation Lionheart Homecoming] On 8 February 2023, SCDF deployed the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent to Trkiye to assist in disaster rescue efforts in the aftermath of the Trkiye-Syria earthquake. The OLH contingent, comprising 68 members and four canines, had safely returned to Singapore early this morning (18 Feb). The contingent members were received by Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, and His Excellency Mehmet Burin Gnenli, Turkish Ambassador to Singapore at Changi Airport. Families and loved ones were also present to warmly welcome them home.In his welcome address, Minister Shanmugam commended the OLH contingent for their unwavering efforts in conducting extensive search and rescue operations across multiple rescue sites in Trkiye. He also expressed his appreciation and gratitude to the families and loved ones for supporting the contingent members during their 10-day deployment. On behalf of Trkiye, His Excellency Mehmet Burin Gnenli thanked the OLH contingent for rendering assistance to the communities affected by the earthquake. He also acknowledged the contingent members for carrying out a safe and successful mission. To our Lifesavers, thank you for your commitment and dedication to service. Welcome home! SCDF would like to express our appreciation to Singapore Embassy in Ankara and the stanbul Airport for the assistance rendered to the OLH contingents deployment in Trkiye. We would also like to thank Singapore Airlines, Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore, Changi Airport Group, and Turkish Airlines for facilitating the contingents flight and logistical arrangements on short notice. The help that has been provided to us has been pivotal in supporting the OLH contingents deployment to, and return from Trkiye.

caption: [Update 14: Standing down of Operation Lionheart]As Operation Lionheart (OLH) draws to a close, the 68-member contingent is preparing to depart from Trkiye later today (17 Feb). A few days prior to the departure, the OLH contingent met with the Trkiye National Medical Rescue Team, otherwise known as the Ulusal Medikal Kurtarma Ekibi (UMKE). The UMKE specialises in medical disaster relief and has been rendering assistance to Trkiye following the massive earthquake. During the meeting, the OLH contingent contributed medical supplies such as trauma equipment and medical drugs, as well as other necessities like food rations, thermal wear and tents.Ambassador Jonathan Tow, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Singapore to the Republic of Trkiye also visited the OLH contingent at their Base of Operation as the OLH contingent were making preparations to stand down. The Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) suit worn by the OLH contingent represents an important element of identity among us and our commitment to saving lives. The USAR suits were presented to the locals as a gesture of our friendship and solidarity with them as they move forward to rebuild their lives following this devastating earthquake. Although the OLH contingent is leaving Trkiye, the people of Trkiye will always be in our hearts and minds

caption: The SCDF annual statistics for Emergency Medical Services (EMS), Fire Incidents and Fire Safety Enforcement for Year 2022 were released today. In a nutshell: 1. The total number of EMS calls increased by 20.2% in 2022. There was an increase of 20.2% and 27.5% in emergency and non-emergency calls respectively, due in part to the multiple COVID-19 waves of infection. 2. SCDF responded to 1,799 fires in 2022, a slight decline of 2.4% or 45 fire incidents from 1,844 in 2021. There were 935 fires in residential buildings (private and public), accounting for 52.0% of the total fire calls in 2022. 3. Fires caused by unattended cooking and electrical origins remained the leading causes of fires in residential buildings in 2022, accounting for 37% and 24% of fires in residential buildings respectively. 4. SCDF stepped up the number of fire safety enforcement checks in 2022 with the easing of COVID-19 restrictions and resumption of business activities. SCDF conducted a total of 12,792 fire safety enforcement checks, an increase of 15.5% from 11,075 in 2021.More useful information on fire safety can be found in the latest edition of the Civil Defence Emergency Handbook. caption: [Update 1: SCDF Operation Lionheart Mission to Trkiye]An advance team of 20 SCDF officers from the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent will be departing for Adana, Trkiye at 2:05 a.m. today (8 Feb), to assist in the disaster rescue efforts in the aftermath of the Trkiye-Syria earthquake.Led by LTC Lok Wee Keong, commander of SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), the advance team comprises 14 DART rescuers, four paramedic specialists and a Full-time National Serviceman (NSF) doctor. The team was at HQ SCDF yesterday morning to begin their pre-departure briefing and preparation. They will be carrying a slew of portable Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) equipment such as cutting/breaking/lifting equipment, life detection devices and fibre-optic scopes, and this will allow the team to be quickly deployed to affected areas for USAR operations.Yesterday evening, His Excellency Mehmet Burin Gnenli, Turkish Ambassador to Singapore, visited SCDF Headquarters and met up with the OLH contingent to express his gratitude and appreciation to the team. Prior to the team's departure, Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, and COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF, were at the airport to send the team off. We would like to thank Singapore Airlines for facilitating the flight arrangements on short notice. We wish our OLH contingent a safe and successful mission.

With the completion of these two phases, officers may look forward to more advanced training facilities which will offer a wider range of realistic and challenging training scenarios. caption: [Fire @ Block 699, Hougang Street 52]At about 2:30 p.m. today (23 Nov), SCDF was alerted to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, thick black smoke was emitting from a living room of a unit on the 5th floor. Firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station conducted forcible entry to gain access into the unit. The fire, which was confined to the living room, was extinguished with a water jet.While the firefighting operation was ongoing, SCDF rescued two persons from the kitchen and carried them out of the smoke-logged unit. The two persons were conveyed by SCDF ambulances to Singapore General Hospital and KK Womens & Children Hospital for smoke inhalation. About 20 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire had likely originated from a personal mobility device (PMD) that was charging in the living room. SCDF would like to remind the public on the prevention of PMD/PAB fires, including not to charge batteries for an extended period of time or overnight. Do not purchase or use non-original batteries. See the accompanying infographic for more fire safety tips.

caption: Following the conclusion of a 24-hour assessment by a team of International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) assessors, we are pleased to announce that the SCDF Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) framework for our ORNS Rescue and Medical Units (RU/MU) has been successfully accredited! SCDF is honoured to be the first organisation in the Asia-Pacific region to undergo this accreditation exercise and have its USAR framework for ORNS units recognised by the INSARAG. About 300 ORNS personnel from the SCDF 21 RU/MU were involved in this accreditation exercise held at the Home Team Tactical Centre over the weekend, where their USAR capabilities were tested in both day and night operations involving complex height rescue, cutting, rigging and lifting operations. LTC (NS) Jahan De Silva Din Abdullah, Commander, 21 RU, was proud of his unit's effort and contributions in attaining this achievement for SCDF - Our training and hard work over the past three years, and overcoming the challenges posed by the pandemic, have come to fruition.Mr Mohd Halimi Taib, Team Lead of the Technical Recognition Group from INSARAG, complimented the ORNS Unit for having shown "a high level of competency and skills proficiency. This enabled the unit to have good command, control and coordination of the multiple and concurrent rescue and medical scenarios that the unit was tested over the 24-hour assessment". Our deep appreciation goes out to our ORNSmen without whom this achievement would not be possible. Thank you for your strong commitment in serving the nation! TheLifeSavingForce SCDFcelebratesNS55

caption: [Mass Fire Evacuation Drill @ KTPH]The Mass Fire Evacuation Drill (MFED) launching ceremony took place at Khoo Teck Puat Hospital (KTPH) earlier today. Organised by the National Fire And Emergency Preparedness Council - NFEC with participation from Yishun Health and SCDF, this much anticipated campaign resumed after a two-year hiatus due to COVID-19. The launching ceremony kicked off with a simulated fire in one of the wards. Upon activation, the hospital's Company Emergency Response Team (CERT) sprung into action to provide immediate firefighting response and casualty evacuation. Upon SCDFs arrival, the CERT continue to work together with the SCDF firefighters to extinguish the fire and ensure safe evacuation of all patients.About 310 premises and more than 58,000 participants will be conducting MFEDs in their respective premises during this month-long campaign. Such MFEDs are essential in validating the response plans and evacuation procedures of the premises, to ensure that everyone is prepared to take the necessary action in the event of an emergency. caption: [Neighbours help others to safely evacuate during a fire at Blk 866 Yishun St 81]On the evening of 23 July 2022, two Good Samaritans worked together to safely evacuate their fellow neighbours at the above-mentioned location.Mr Malik Maksudi had just reached home when he heard cries for help. He proceeded down the block and saw smoke and flames coming out of a unit on the 4th floor. Mr John Wu, Vice-Chairman of the National Fire And Emergency Preparedness Council, who is also a resident of the block, sprung into action alongside Mr Malik.Upon arriving at the affected unit, the duo successfully evacuated a person who was still inside and other occupants from neighbouring units. The probable cause of the fire was determined to be due to electrical origin in a bedroom of the affected unit. Such fires can be avoided: Do not continue to use electrical appliances that are faulty or have signs of damage to the wires. Do not overload an electrical socket.Yesterday, Mr Malik was presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. caption: [Exercise Rambo 2022]A total of 259 Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS) from 42 Rescue Unit (RU) and 42 Medical Unit (MU), took part in a gruelling, 12-hour long exercise earlier today at the Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC).In the Rescue Unit/Medical Unit Proficiency Assessment (codenamed Exercise Rambo), our ORNS will undergo a series of simulated scenarios specifically designed to rigorously test and evaluate their competencies in handling large-scale and prolonged urban search and rescue (USAR) operations. Such exercises are crucial in ensuring the operational readiness of our ORNS in responding to major emergencies.The ORNS are tasked in various individual roles, such as rescuers, medical support and service support personnel. As a unit, they are required to conduct USAR operations in collapsed structures based on the United Nation's International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) requirements. The ORNS were tested on their ability to perform cutting, breaking, and lifting operations, and render medical assistance to casualties at the incident site.This exercise capped-off the 42 RU's 5th year of In-Camp Training (ICT). The ORNS had sacrificed their personal time to ensure the success of the exercise. We thank them for responding to the call of duty, and being ready to protect and save lives and property for a safe Singapore. TheLifeSavingForceSCDFcelebratesNS55

We have put in place measures to manage the increase in EMS Calls. Refrain from calling 995 if you are not suffering any life-threatening or emergency medical conditions.By doing so, SCDF can continue to provide swift conveyance to those who require our emergency medical services. See pictures for more details.

caption: [Community Lifesavers on Wheels]This afternoon, the SCDF-Ninja Van AED-on-Wheels programme was officially launched by Ms Sun Xueling, Minister of State for Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Social and Family Development.50 delivery vehicles from have been equipped with Automated External Defibrillators (AEDs), sponsored by COSEM Safety and Security Services Pte Ltd. Ninja Van Singapore has also equipped these 50 vehicles with a fire extinguisher and a first aid kit. To prepare them for their role as Community Lifesavers, 50 Ninja Van drivers have been trained by SCDF to administer Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), applying AED, conduct basic firefighting and administer first aid.The AED-on-Wheels programme equips vehicles on the move with an AED, in support of SCDFs Save-A-Life initiative. The other companies who are onboard this programme are: Strides Taxi (formerly SMRT Taxi), Grab and ComfortDelGro.Drivers are alerted to cardiac arrest emergencies and also minor fires within a 1.5 kilometre radius of their vehicle's location through SCDF's myResponder app.During the launch, an active AED-on-Wheels taxi driver from was also awarded the SCDF Community First Responder Award. Mr Elson Sim Kong Thong had responded and assisted in two minor fires and two cardiac arrest incidents last year.SCDF warmly welcomes Ninja Van and its drivers to the Lifesaver family. To prepare them for their role as Community Lifesavers, 50 Ninja Van drivers have been trained by SCDF to administer Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), applying AED, conduct basic firefighting and administer first aid. The AED-on-Wheels programme equips vehicles on the move with an AED, in support of SCDF’s Save-A-Life initiative. The other companies who are onboard this programme are: Strides Taxi (formerly SMRT Taxi), Grab and ComfortDelGro. Drivers are alerted to cardiac arrest emergencies and also minor fires within a 1.5 kilometre radius of their vehicle's location through SCDF's myResponder app. During the launch, an active AED-on-Wheels taxi driver was also awarded the SCDF Community First Responder Award for responding and assisting in two minor fires and two cardiac arrest incidents last year. SCDF warmly welcomes Ninja Van and its drivers to the Lifesaver family. #ANationofLifesavers

caption: [Geylang Serai Community Resilience Day]On Saturday, 2 July 2022, about 500 participants attended the Geylang Serai Community Resilience (CR) Day, organised by 2nd SCDF Division in partnership with the People's Association (PA) and the Geylang Serai Community Emergency and Engagement (C2E) Committee. The CR Day aims to impart and equip members of the public with Emergency Preparedness (EP) skills and knowledge such as Improvised First Aid Skills (IFAS), conducting Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), usage of an Automated External Defibrillator (AED), and how to use a fire extinguisher, as well as household fire safety tips.As part of the CR Day, participants will also learn how to respond when the Public Warning System is activated and where to find the nearest Civil Defence Public Shelters.Upon being equipped with these life-saving skills, the public is encouraged to step forward and register as Community First Responders (CFRs) to assist those in need of help during emergencies. CFRs are vital in enabling our community to stay strong and resilient by assisting in grassroots emergency response efforts with the respective C2Es.SCDF, PA and C2E Committees plan to conduct a series of CR Day programmes annually across the four SCDF land Divisions. In the meantime, you can also join us in paving the way towards building ANationofLifesavers by learning lifesaving skills through the Community Emergency and Preparedness Programme (CEPP). You can find out more through the link in our bio!

caption: [SCDF DART - UK ISAR Exercise 2022]Earlier this week, we welcomed our friends from the UK International Search and Rescue (ISAR) team for a joint urban search and rescue exercise. Held at the Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC) at Mandai from 28 - 30 June, the exercise was conducted together with rescuers from SCDF's elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART). The exercise saw the participants conducting a number of challenging exercise scenarios such as search and rescue of a collapsed building, chemical plant incident and a complex height rescue exercise. The UK ISAR team was led by Commander Russ Gauden. He shared that "The facility (at HTTC) gave a huge test of endurance, skill and attributes for UK ISAR. SCDF are a world leading team and the opportunity to train and exercise alongside them gave UK ISAR colleagues and myself a huge sense of pride." Singapore's hot and humid weather was also an element of challenge for the British rescuers as the climate here is unlike their home country, but we salute them for their perseverance and stamina throughout the exercise! On top of the hands-on exercise to test their response capabilities, a sharing session was also held where the experts from UK discussed topics relating to search and rescue, such as disaster victim identification.The joint exercise was an enriching opportunity for both parties to work alongside and learn from each other, in our common mission of protecting and saving lives. To many more years of partnership! thelifesavingforce: MX Aidil and LCP Syukri, SCDF Corporate Communications Department

caption: [Fire @ Block 682 Hougang Avenue 4]At approximately 9.50pm yesterday (1 July), SCDF responded to a fire at the above-mentioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was raging and thick black smoke was emitting from a 3rd floor unit. The fire involved contents of a bedroom. Firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station donned breathing apparatus sets and extinguished the fire with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the entire unit was affected by heat and smoke damage.One occupant from the affected unit had evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival. caption: [25th Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Ceremony]After undergoing seven months of rigorous training, 36 officer cadets from the 25th RCC were commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy this morning.The RCC commissioning ceremony is a significant milestone that marks the transition of these 36 individuals, including 25 Full-time National Servicemen, into SCDF Senior Officers. As Senior Officers, their tasks include leading a team to respond to a wide range of incidents such as firefighting, rescue and Hazardous Materials. This RCC also included international trainees for the first time in two years due to the pandemic. Hailing from the BFRD - Brunei Fire Rescue Department, the three participants now join the ranks of other BFRD Senior Officers who have graduated from SCDFs training programmes.In a speech delivered by Mr Zhulkarnain Bin Abdul Rahim, the Deputy Chairperson of the Government Parliamentary Committee (Home Affairs and Law), he acknowledged the strong support of family members and friends of the cadets in helping them to reach this significant milestone. He also spoke about the great responsibilities to be shouldered by the newly minted Senior Officers, and urged them to always prioritise the well-being and safety of the people they lead.On the very same training grounds where months of learning and intense training took place, the cadets stood proudly and were officially commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers. Congratulations to the 25th RCC! We wish them all the best as they venture forth in their journey with the Life Saving Force. ANationOfLifesavers

caption: [Fire @ Block 218 Marsiling Crescent]At approximately 10.40pm yesterday (22 June), SCDF responded to a fire at the above-mentioned location.The fire involved contents of a bedroom in a 2nd floor unit. Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was raging and thick black smoke was emitting from the unit. Firefighters from Woodlands Fire Station donned breathing apparatus sets and extinguished the fire with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the entire unit was affected by heat and smoke damage.About 60 people from neighbouring units were evacuated by the Police as a precautionary measure. Two police officers also rescued two toddlers who were found conscious in the living room of the affected unit prior to SCDFs arrival. The two toddlers were conveyed to KK Women's and Children's Hospital by two SCDF ambulances.We understand that after the fire started, a member of the public had attempted to force open the door of the affected unit to rescue the two toddlers. SCDF will be reaching out to the person to commend him for his quick-thinking and prompt action in attempting to rescue the toddlers.The cause of fire is under investigation.

Firefighters from Sengkang Fire Station donned breathing apparatus sets and conducted forcible entry to gain access into the unit. No one was in the unit.The fire, which involved the contents of kitchen, was extinguished using a water jet. A dog was found in the living room of the unit and was rescued by SCDF. The dog was handed back to the owner. About 10 people from the affected block were evacuated by SCDF. There were no reported injuries. The fire was largely confined to the kitchen and the cause of the fire is under investigation.

caption: [Marymount Community Resilience Day]Earlier today (5 June), the Marymount Community Resilience (CR) Day, held at Bishan North Shopping Mall was launched by Ms Gan Siow Huang, Advisor to Marymount SMC grassroots organisations. Marymount CR Day marks the first time a fully physical CR Day was held since the easing of Covid-19 safe management measures.The CR Day programme, organised in partnership with Peoples Association (PA), National Fire and Emergency Preparedness Council (NFEC), and Community Emergency and Engagement (C2E) Committees, aims to impart skills such as Improvised First Aid, Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR), Automated External Defibrillator (AED), using a fire extinguisher, as well as raising awareness on various fire safety tips. Participants can also learn about the Public Warning System and Civil Defence Shelters.Once equipped with these life-saving skills, the public are encouraged to step forward and register as Community First Responders (CFRs) to assist those in distress in times of an emergency.During Marymount CR Day, 8 persons were presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award (CFRA) and 3 persons were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award (CLA). The CFRA is presented to members of the public who stepped forward to render assistance to others in distress and/or save property. The CLA is presented to members of the public whose actions involved an element of self-risk and/or contributed to saving lives.You too can learn EP skills in the physical session of the SCDFs Community Emergency Preparedness Programme or attend its e-modules session online at

caption: [Opening of Lifesavers' Connect Hub at Kallang Fire Station]Did you know that besides learning Emergency Preparedness skills, SCDF volunteer leaders also receive training on leadership and public speaking skills?Yesterday (31 May), the Lifesavers' Connect Hub (LCH) at Kallang Fire Station (KFS) was officially opened by Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. The LCH will serve as a dedicated space for SCDF volunteer leaders to receive training beyond lifesaving skills. With these skills, they will be able to carry out their roles meaningfully as well-rounded volunteers. These volunteer leaders include members of the Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit, as well as student members of the National Civil Defence Cadet Corps and CD Lionhearter Club. The LCH at KFS will host the training for our volunteer leaders while the permanent LCH will be built at Hill Street. Visit the Home Team Volunteer Network through the link in our bio to find out more on how you can be a SCDF volunteer!ANationOfLifesavers

caption: [Rescue @ 18, Defu Avenue 2] At about 1.05pm today (27 May), SCDF was activated for a rescue incident Involving a man that was trapped under a large metal cylindrical pipe between a trailer and a lorry. Arriving first at the scene, SCDF firefighters and Emergency Medical Services from Paya Lebar Fire Station immediately conducted an assessment on the trapped man and promptly rendered medical assistance to stabilise him. Rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) were also activated, and working together with the fire station crew, they used two air lifting bags to lift the pipe. An air lifting bag is a thin and lightweight piece of rescue equipment that can be used in confined spaces, where bulkier rescue equipment would not be able to be deployed. When compressed air is filled into the air lifting bag, it expands and enables rescuers to lift, spread or create space between two objects, thereby facilitating the rescue operation. Once the injured man was freed, an SCDF ambulance conveyed him to Tan Tock Seng Hospital.

caption: The SCDF Emergency Medical Services (EMS) community gathered together earlier this week for the inaugural launch of the SCDF EMS Week. caption: [SCDF Celebrates NS55]Here in SCDF, serving National Service (NS) goes beyond being in a frontline unit. There are many vocations that allow both our Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS) and full-time National Servicemen (NSF) to contribute to the best that they could. Meet CPL(NS) Burhan Jumadi, an ORNSman who used to serve his 2-year full-time NS as a Multimedia Specialist in the Media Production Unit (MPU) of SCDF's Corporate Communications Department from 2019 to 2020. During his NSF days with MPU, CPL(NS) Burhan was actively involved in MPU's camera and lighting team to produce SCDF in-house media content for educational and branding purposes. His most memorable involvement was during the 2019 Singapore-Global Firefighters & Paramedics Challenge (SGFPC). CPL(NS) Burhan, together with his team, put their heads together for the intensive planning on the camera angle for the live streaming of SGFPC online. And it was a smashing success winning the hearts and accolades of netizens!With CPL(NS) Burhan's past experience in the Audio Visual (AV) Industry prior to his NS enlistment, being in MPU gave him the golden opportunity to put his skills and experience into good use. It also allowed him to stay abreast of latest developments, including building up his social network in the media industry.Today, CPL(NS) Burhan still keeps in touch with his former NSF batchmates and he is confident that their friendship will persist for many years to come. "In MPU, it doesn't matter whether you are junior or senior individuals. What matters is the rich and fruitful journey you'll embark together in your 2 years as NSFs with the team".This year, as we celebrate 55 years of NS in Singapore, we in SCDF pay tribute to the effort and dedication of Singaporeans who are serving as well as those who had served NS across vocations. THANK YOU for your service to our nation! {Stay tune for the coverage of more NS vocations in our subsequent series.}

caption: [SCDF rescues 14 cats from fire]On 21 April 2022 at about 8.30am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at Block 422 Fajar Road. caption: [Fire @ Kusu Island]At approximately 6.30pm yesterday on 17 April in the midst of a heavy downpour, SCDFs marine and land-based firefighting forces responded to a fire at Kusu island, one of the offshore islands on the southern coast of Singapore. SCDF despatched a Marine Rescue Vessel (MRV) and a Rapid Response Fire Vessel (RFV) from Brani Marine Fire Station and West Coast Marine Fire Station. An additional firefighting crew from Marina Bay Fire Station was also despatched and responded aboard the RFV. Upon SCDF's arrival at the island, the fire was raging at a cluster of shrines located on top of a hill. Using the MRV as a water pump, the firefighters laid a vast number of hoses from the jetty to the top of the hill, covering a distance of about 520 meters. The fire was extinguished with two water jets within an hour of SCDF's arrival on the island.There were no reported injuries. Damping down* operations are ongoing. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent any potential rekindling of fire from hot burnt surfaces.

caption: [Four Sport Singapore staff successfully resuscitate a cardiac arrest patient] On the afternoon of 15 Feb 2022, staff Mr Guo Ze, Mr Luo Shiwei, Mr Kow Heng Bee and Ms Lee Pei Shan were alerted to a collapsed man at Kallang Basin Swimming Complex.Upon assessing that the man was not breathing and had no pulse, the team immediately conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and used an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) before SCDF's arrival. caption: On 1 April 2022 at about 6.35am, SCDF was alerted to a road traffic accident near the junction of Lok Yang Way and First Lok Yang Road. Upon SCDF's arrival at the incident scene, a passenger bus was found overturned on its side. Another passenger bus had rammed into a fence by the roadside and a man was pinned in the driver's seat. Firefighters from Jurong Fire Station used hydraulic rescue equipment to free the man. The man was subsequently pronounced dead at the scene by an SCDF paramedic. As there were multiple casualties involved in this accident, the first-arriving SCDF paramedic established a triaging system to prioritise the casualties according to the severity of their injuries. Casualties with severe injuries were treated and conveyed to the hospitals as priority. Additional ambulances and medical resources were also dispatched to support the ongoing operation. A Mass Decontamination Vehicle (MDV) from SCDF's Special Rescue Unit (SRU) was also activated to the incident. Responders from the SRU, comprising Full-time National Servicemen, configured their MDV into a casualty conveyance vehicle. The MDV subsequently conveyed 14 casualties to Ng Teng Fong General Hospital.A total of 37 casualties were conveyed by SCDF to Ng Teng Fong General Hospital and National University Hospital.

caption: [Commemorating a Decade of Marine Transformation]On this day a decade ago, SCDFs Marine Division (MD) was officially established. Fast forward 10 years and here we are today Bigger. Faster. Stronger. A commemorative event was held earlier this morning to mark this significant milestone. Gracing the event as the Guest-of-Honour was Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS) for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development.SCDFs MD would not be where we are today without the hard work of our committed marine officers, including NSFs and ORNSmen. To honour the efforts of our pioneer officers who took on the challenge of building up this Division since 2012, a specially designed Marine Medallion was presented by Assoc Prof Faishal to ten long serving officers.In attendance at the ceremony were representatives from related agencies such as Police Coast Guard, , , Maritime Security Task Force and . Each of these agencies have supported the MD over the past decade.As we journey ahead, MD will, among other things, be pursuing the use of more advanced and unmanned technologies in fire and rescue operations. We also look forward to expand our fleet of next generation marine vessels with enhanced capabilities, as well as establishing a new Division HQ and a third Marine Fire Post at Punggol by 2025. Psst. If you want to find out more about MD's transformation in the past decade, please visit the Civil Defence Heritage Gallery located at Central Fire Station at 62 Hill Street.SCDFMarineTurns10ADecadeOfTransformation

caption: [Three Good Samaritans assisted during a fire at Block 29 Chai Chee Avenue] On the morning of 8 Mar 2022, three Good Samaritans assisted during a fire at the above-mentioned location. caption: [Exercise Bluewhale Mar 2022] Earlier this week, SCDF conducted a marine emergency response exercise in the southern part of Singapore. The exercise was supported by and The exercise scenario involved the release of a chemical agent (CA) onboard a ferry carrying 60 passengers. Many passengers who were exposed to the toxic CA vapour started convulsing and vomiting, and one passenger fell overboard in a bid to escape the fumes. Such a challenging scenario is important as it allows SCDF to test and fine-tune its ops coordination between its Marine Division and Land Divisions , including validating and updating its operational plans and procedures with related agencies. During the exercise, about 20 emergency and supporting vehicles, including marine vessels from SCDF and related agencies, were deployed. Check out the pictures on SCDFs operational response to such an incident! By the way, did you know that it has been almost a decade since SCDF set up its marine firefighting and rescue capability? caption: On 29 Nov 2021 at about 6.15pm, six Good Samaritans and an SCDF Operationally Ready National Serviceman (ORNS) saved the life of a man who had a cardiac arrest and had fallen along the staircase entrance at Marymount MRT Station.Corporal (NS) Vincent Yong De Hao was on his way home after completing his operational standby at Bishan Fire Station as part of his In-Camp Training, when he noticed the cardiac arrest victim and sprung into action to assess him. Eldercare facility colleagues Ms Jacqueline Teo Mei Ling and Ms Kam Siew Yuen who were passing by, joined Corporal (NS) Vincent to render assistance.SMRT Senior Station Manager (SSM) Mr Gary Tan Kian Kok & Assistant Station Manager (ASM) Mr Shakirin Bin Sarip, who were on duty at the Marymount MRT Station, were alerted of the incident. Upon assessing the situation, SSM Gary immediately grabbed an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) from the passenger service counter, while ASM Shakirin called 995.Working as a team, the five lifesavers took turns to perform CPR-AED.Shortly after SCDFs arrival, off-duty nurses Ms Hannah Thang Hui Li & Ms Carmelita B. Lumayag joined the other Good Samaritans in conducting CPR-AED and assisting SCDFs Emergency Medical Services.Yesterday morning, these community first responders were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award by COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander, 1st SCDF Division. Corporal (NS) Vincent will be commended with the SCDF Service Excellence Award.You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDFs Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP) or attend its e-modules session online at From L to R: COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander, 1st SCDF Division, Ms Kam Siew Yuen, Ms Hannah Thang Hui Li, SSM Gary Tan Kian Kok, Ms Jacqueline Teo Mei Ling, ASM Shakirin Bin Sarip, COL Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department. Not in picture: Ms Carmelita B. Lumayag, Corporal (NS) Vincent Yong De Hao.
cleaned_caption: On 29 Nov 2021 at about 6.15pm, six Good Samaritans and an SCDF Operationally Ready National Serviceman (ORNS) saved the life of a man who had a cardiac arrest and had fallen along the staircase entrance at Marymount MRT Station. Corporal (NS) was on his way home after completing his operational standby at Bishan Fire Station as part of his In-Camp Training, when he noticed the cardiac arrest victim and sprung into action to assess him. Eldercare facility colleagues joined Corporal (NS) to render assistance. SMRT Senior Station Manager (SSM) & Assistant Station Manager (ASM), who were on duty at the Marymount MRT Station, were alerted of the incident. Upon assessing the situation, SSM immediately grabbed an Automated External Defibrillator (AED) from the passenger service counter, while ASM called 995. Working as a team, the five lifesavers took turns to perform CPR-AED. Shortly after SCDF's arrival, off-duty nurses joined the other Good Samaritans in conducting CPR-AED and assisting SCDF's Emergency Medical Services. Yesterday morning, these community first responders were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award by COL, Commander, 1st SCDF Division. Corporal (NS) will be commended with the SCDF Service Excellence Award. You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP) or attend its e-modules session online. From L to R: COL, Commander, 1st SCDF Division, members of the lifesaving team. Not in picture: off-duty nurses, Corporal (NS).

caption: Yesterday (13 Dec 2021), five members of the public were awarded the Community Lifesaver Award (CLA), in recognition of their public-spiritedness and gallant efforts in two separate incidents. The two incidents involved 1 a residential unit on fire and 2 a cardiac arrest victim.1 In the first incident, Mr Goh Boon Hong was alerted to his neighbours cries for help when a fire broke out in her kitchen. With the help of 2 other Community First Responders (CFRs), Mr Goh extinguished the fire using a fire extinguisher from his home before SCDFs arrival. I bought an extinguisher because I dont know when Ill need it, said Mr Goh.2 In the second incident, Mr Darryl Lee responded to an alert on his myResponder app notifying him of a cardiac arrest case. Upon his arrival at the incident site, he saw a group of CFRs performing CPR on the victim. He proceeded to assist by administering oxygen to the victim.I was very nervous, but I did what I could, said Mr Darryl when recounting the incident. I would give (Mr Darryl) full marks for his assistance that day. We couldnt have done it without him, said Dr Bernard Cheong, one of the other award recipients who resuscitated the cardiac arrest victim before SCDFs arrival. The award was presented by COL Goh Boon Han, Commander 4th SCDF Division, during an award presentation ceremony at HQ 4th SCDF Division. Kudos to the 5 Good Samaritans who stepped forward! Head to our SCDF Facebook page for more details of their collective CFR efforts!To learn more on what to do in such emergencies, join the online module of the SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness Programme via the link in our bio or contact one of the four SCDF Division HQs to register for a practical class. caption: Besides SCDFs microsite and FB, our SCDF e-magazine, Rescue 995, is now on Instagram too! caption: On the morning of 3 Dec 2021, 19 people were recognised with the SCDF Community First Responder Award (CFRA) and Community Lifesaver Award (CLA) for their life saving actions during two separate cardiac arrest incidents. On 27 Sep 2021, staff Mr Muhammad Adlan Bin Hasan Basri, Mr Steven Ismail Bin Muhammad, Mr Henry Tan Kim Heng and Mr Abdul Naqeeb Bin Abdul Latiff were alerted when an instructor had collapsed from cardiac arrest at Heartbeat. The team conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and used an Automated External Defibrillator to successfully resuscitate the instructor before SCDF's arrival. In another incident on 7 Oct 2021, a worker had suffered from cardiac arrest at Pasir Ris Sport Centre. 15 people came together and conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and used an Automated External Defibrillator until SCDF's arrival. The 15 people are staff Mr Steven Ong How Tiong, Mr Terence Yong Chen Ngiap, Mr Patrick Chan Lee Chong, Ms Norsidah Sheila Hassan, Mr Muhammad Shahir Bin Hamzah, Mr Chan Kok Hong, Mr Fred Leong Chong Wah, Mr Danny Yau Lay Swee, Mr Abdul Rahman Bin Salim, Mr Vincent Fong Peng Yuen, Ms Cecilia Sau Fong Chan, Mr John Lee Say Kheng, and members of public Mr Darren Tan Chun Yong, Mr Marcus Chia Ying Han and Mr Marvel Chua Tze-An. The awards were presented by COL Chew Keng Tok, Commander, 2nd SCDF Division. Kudos to the 19 Good Samaritans who stepped forward! You too can learn basic firefighting, first aid and CPR-AED in the physical session of the SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness Programme (CEPP) or attend its e-modules session online at CommunityFirstResponders CommunityLifesaversANationofLifesavers OurCFRsOurHeroes

caption: You might have seen videos circulating online a few weeks ago of smoke billowing dramatically out from the SLE underpass. What you didn't see was the teamwork of a dynamic duo to save the day...On 2 November 2021, during the early evening rush hour traffic at about 5.00pm, two gentlemen rescued a driver from a car that was on fire at the exit 1 slip road of the underpass along SLE (towards BKE).One of these gentlemen, Mr Johnson Chia Yong Lee, was driving along SLE when he saw a car careen across the road and hit the left wall of the underpass. He saw black smoke emitting from the damaged car and immediately stopped his car. Driven by a sense of duty, he got out of his car and rushed over to help.When he reached the affected car, a fire was developing within it. The driver was still in the burning car and in a daze! Mr Johnson opened the driver's door and swiftly brought the dazed driver out of the car. Another gentleman, Mr Azlee Bin Abd Shukor, was driving a van when he spotted black smoke and flames in the SLE underpass. Then, he saw Mr Johnson waving frantically for assistance. Realizing the precarious situation, he stopped his van alongside Mr Johnson.Working as a team, the duo brought the dazed driver into Mr Azlee's van. They then drove further down the road towards safety, away from the intense heat and smoke of the burning car.For their gallant rescue and timely intervention, Mr Johnson and Mr Azlee were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander 3rd SCDF Division, today.Kudos to Mr Johnson and Mr Azlee, our brave heroes! caption: [Community Resilience Day @ 1st Div] On 30 October 2021, 1st SCDF Division held the first ever Community Resilience (CR) Day in collaboration with and QueenstownC2E Committee. The CR Day saw approximately 150 participants tuning in through zoom while about 40 participants were physically present (in accordance to prevailing SMMs) to learn essential life-saving skills on what to do during an emergency situation. Participants were trained in first aid, CPR & AED, and fire safety at home through a fun and engaging session led by the SCDF hosts. Parliamentary Secretary, Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth & Ministry of Social and Family Development, and Queenstown Grassroots Advisor Mr Eric Chua graced the event. In his address, he highlighted the importance of Community First Responders and the crucial role they play in lending a helping hand to others in times of emergency.This is vital in enabling our community to stay strong.Amidst the ongoing COVID-19 situation, SCDF will be imparting Emergency Preparedness skills in a series of hybrid Community Resilience Days to be rolled out by the four SCDF Divisions, in accordance to prevailing SMMs.In the meantime, do join these Queenstown residents in paving the way towards building ANationofLifesavers and learning lifesaving skills through the Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP). The CEPP is also available online.

caption: [Fire @ No. 86 Geylang Bahru]Earlier today at about 2.35am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the aforementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, the fire was well-alight in two ground floor units of a double storey industrial premises. Firefighters immediately deployed water jets around the exterior of the premises to contain the fire and prevent it from spreading. Simultaneously, forcible entry was conducted to create quick access into the burning units.Once the fire was under control, firefighters wearing breathing apparatus sets proceeded deep into the smoke-logged unit to locate the seat of fire. Firefighters had to exercise extreme caution as the second floor mezzanine level had already collapsed.The fire involving contents of a plumbing services workshop across two units was extinguished by SCDF in about two hours. The adjacent units sustained heat and smoke damages.SCDF deployed 17 emergency vehicles and about 60 firefighters to the incident. At the height of the firefighting operation, four water jets and an Unmanned Firefighting Machine (UFM) were deployed. A Combined Platform Ladder (CPL) was also utilised for aerial monitoring of the incident.A firefighter, a Full-Time National Serviceman (NSF), experienced slight smoke inhalation. He was conveyed to Singapore General Hospital and has since been discharged. There were no other reported injuries. SCDF is currently performing damping down* operations.*Damping down refers to the application of water to wet burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent any potential rekindle of fire from the hot burnt surfaces.

caption: Yesterday, SCDF participated in the Ferry Rescue Exercise (FEREX), an annual exercise conducted by . caption: [Decommissioning of SCDF's pioneer vessels]When SCDF took over the marine firefighting and rescue functions from Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) on 1 April 2012, we also took over the operation of two Marine Fire Vessels (MFVs). Deployed in numerous firefighting and rescue incidents, standby as well as exercises, these MFVs played an instrumental role in the formative years of SCDF Marine Division.Right before sunset on 3rd August 2021, Firefighter 1 and Firefighter 2 were officially decommissioned in a ceremony. This is the first time that SCDF has held a decommissioning ceremony for our vessels and it was attended by a contingent from Marine Division and fire stations. Against the setting sun, the blue ensign flags from the two MFVs were lowered to symbolise the halt to their operation. It was a formal and solemn ceremony, befitting the retirement of our pioneer vessels.The decommissioning ceremony was followed by a send-off on 4th August 2021. The send-off included a water salute for the MFVs as they passed through the channel, with marine personnel waving their final goodbyes. The decommissioning and send-off of these MFVs mark a bittersweet moment for us. While we are sad to bid goodbye to our pioneer vessels, we are glad to know that their legacy have led to a new generation of state-of-the-art firefighting and rescue vessels, which stand ready to continue to keep Singapore waters in safe hands.

caption: [Fire @ 70 West Coast Ferry Road] At about 4.40pm today, SCDF responded to a fire at the aforementioned address. The fire involved a berthed tugboat. caption: In times of emergency, would you know how to react? If your answer is no, why not consider joining our Community Emergency Preparedness Programme (CEPP). CEPP focuses on equiping participants with knowledge on core lifesaving skills and essential emergency procedures, so that you can help others during emergencies. The CEPP syllabus consists of 3 tiers: 'I am Safe' (Tier 1), 'Response Ready' (Tier 2) and 'Lifesaver' (Tier 3). Tier 1 and 2 are available online as e-modules, so you can learn them at your own convenience. Upon successful completion of the online module in Tier 2, you can then sign up for the practical lessons in Tier 2 and 3, which are held in person. Do make sure to complete the Tier 2 e-module before booking a Tier 2 practical lesson at the Division HQ closest to you!Find out more about CEPP at: TogetherANationOfLifesaversTheLifeSavingForceCommunityFirstResponder
