caption: [SCDF conducts workshop on Urban Search and Rescue for international participants]Recently, SCDF, with support from the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA), conducted a workshop on the International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) Guidelines 2020 for the Asia Pacific (AP) region.The virtual event was attended by about 120 international participants from the INSARAG Network, including government officials and national civil defence organisations. The opening remarks were delivered by SCDFs Deputy Commissioner (Ops and Resilience), DC Anwar Abdullah, and the INSARAG AP Regional Chair 2021 from BASARNAS Indonesia, Mr Barokna Haulah. During the three-hour session, SCDF speakers introduced participants to the INSARAG community, its systems, and fundamentals of the latest Guidelines - a set of internationally accepted documents that outline the methodology for countries to develop their national urban search and rescue (USAR) response capability. The Guidelines also outline the requirements and standards for international USAR teams to respond to affected countries.The speakers also provided advice on developing a countrys national emergency management framework, which would allow them to better respond to disasters. The workshop concluded with a robust exchange of views during a Q&A session, where participants gleaned a deeper understanding on the practical applications of the Guidelines.We look forward to our continued partnership with the INSARAG network and stand ever ready to contribute to the international Search and Rescue community.

caption: [SCDF X IBM Lifesavers' Innovation Challenge: Call for Code 2021 - Grand Finals] Yesterday, the Grand Finals of the SCDF X IBM Lifesavers' Innovation Challenge: Call for Code 2021, in partnership with Accenture, took place at the Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre. This year, close to 225 students from local tertiary institutions formed teams to participate in the challenge. Before yesterdays event, teams were tasked to submit a 1-minute video pitch along with a code sequence to address one of the problem statements on a Post-Pandemic society, Sustainable Development, and Climate Change. caption: [SCDF X IBM Lifesavers' Innovation Challenge: Call for Code 2021 - Grand Finals] Yesterday, the Grand Finals of the SCDF X IBM Lifesavers' Innovation Challenge: Call for Code 2021, in partnership with Accenture, took place at the Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre. This annual event encourages members of the public to innovate solutions to tackle various issues relating to emergency response and civil defence in Singapore. This year, close to 225 students from local tertiary institutions formed teams to participate in the challenge. Before yesterdays event, teams were tasked to submit a 1-minute video pitch along with a code sequence to address one of the problem statements on a Post-Pandemic society, Sustainable Development, and Climate Change. Six teams eventually made it to todays Grand Finals. The six teams had to pitch their ideas to a panel of judges comprising SCDFs Deputy Commissioner (DC) Teong How Hwa, DC, Future Technology & Public Safety; Tan Jee Toon, Director of IBM Partner Ecosystem Leader (ASEAN); and Cade Tan, Applied Innovation & Ventures Lead (Accenture Southeast Asia). Congratulations to team 'Seviours' for emerging as this years champion! They have been awarded a cash prize of S$10,000 for their winning idea of a system that leverages Internet-of-Things (IoT) sensors, Artifical Intelligence (AI), and automation to enable early and efficient response to high-voltage charging fires. Four other teams were awarded a total cash prize of S$11,000. Each of the top five teams was also awarded up to US$120,000 in IBM cloud credits to develop their projects with IBM. A big thank you to all participants! As we head towards a decade of new frontiers, our civil defence, community resilience and emergency response will need to keep up with the times. Now more than ever, we need innovative solutions so that as ANationOfLifesavers, we are always ready to respond.[In light of the COVID-19 pandemic, Safe Management Measures (SMM) were observed at the event to ensure the safety of all attendees.]

caption: [Memorandum of Understanding between SCDF, SAF and NYP] Earlier today, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF), Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) and Nanyang Polytechnic (NYP) was signed. The signing ceremony was held virtually over Zoom and witnessed by COMR Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF, Major-General Goh Si Hou, Chief of Army and Ms Jeanne Liew, Principal & Chief Executive Officer of NYP.The MoU provides the framework for the enhancement of the professional standards of paramedics, including SCDF paramedics and SAF Military Medical Experts, through a new 12-month Diploma (Conversion) in Paramedic Science and 1200 hours On-The-Job Training Programme (OTP). The diploma provides graduates with strong theoretical foundations and real-world experience essential for frontline paramedics in dealing with increasingly complex pre-hospital health emergencies that require diagnosis and prioritisation of treatment for patients. The OTP will be led by SCDF's National Emergency Medical Services Training Centre for graduates to gain essential hands-on opportunities in real-time emergency ambulance operations under the supervision of senior SCDF paramedics. The MoU was signed by Assistant Commissioner (AC) Yong Meng Wah, Director Emergency Medical Services Department, Chief Army Medical Officer Colonel (COL) (Dr) Lee Wei Ting and Director of NYP's School of Health and Social Sciences Dr Bryan Chua. On the training of a new generation of paramedics, AC Yong said, "This collaboration has allowed us to bring our national pre-hospital emergency care to a level that meets or even surpasses most international standards for quality patient care. I am glad we are levelling up the foundational knowledge and proficiency of the new generation of paramedics and further raising the overall standards of SCDF paramedics."Top (Witnesses): Chief of Army Major-General Goh Si Hou from the SAF, Commissioner Eric Yap from the SCDF and Principal & Chief Executive Officer Ms Jeanne Liew from NYP.Bottom (Signatories): COL (Dr) Lee Wei Ting from the SAF, AC Yong Meng Wah from the SCDF and Dr Bryan Chua from NYP.

caption: "We're really glad that we were able to save him." Ms Sunitha, SCDF Community Lifesaver Award recipient. Yesterday, a husband and wife were commended by SCDF for saving the life of a cardiac arrest patient. On 18 March 2021 at about 6.00pm, Ms Sunitha Palanidurai, an off-duty senior respiratory therapist from Alexandra Hospital, was out for a walk with her husband, Mr Balaji Thangavelu, when they noticed an elderly man being supported by his friend at a nearby multi-purpose hall. The couple approached and realised that the elderly man was in cardiac arrest with no pulse or breathing. They immediately placed him on the floor, conducted Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) and asked passersby to retrieve an Automated External Defibrillator (AED). The elderly man regained his pulse and breathing before the arrival of the SCDFs emergency medical services. For their timely actions, Ms Sunitha and Mr Balaji were awarded the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award, presented by COL Anthony Toh, Commander 4th SCDF Division. Ms Sunitha had learnt the CPR-AED skill in her medical training while Mr Balaji had learnt it as part of his training in the maritime industry. You too can learn CPR-AED skill in SCDF's Community Emergency Prepardness (CEPP) e-modules online at Together ANationOfLifesavers

caption: [Lifesavers on the move]On 28 Jan, the SCDF-Grab AED-on-Wheels programme was officially launched by Associate Professor Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development.50 Grab private hire vehicles are now equipped with AEDs for cardiac arrest cases. They are also equipped with first aid kits and fire extinguishers for other emergencies.To prepare Grab driver-partners for their new lifesaving role, SCDF trained 64 of them on how to perform CPR, apply first aid, and use a fire extinguisher.The AED-on-Wheels programme increases the availability of roving AEDs to facilitate its quick delivery to a cardiac arrest victim, thereby increasing the victims chances of survival. caption: [Workers commended for rescuing boy from ledge]You may have seen a recent viral video of a worker operating a boom lift to rescue a boy from a kitchen ledge. With Mr Jibom directing him and ensuring the path ahead was clear, Mr Dipto carefully steered the machinery with the boom lift down a narrow pathtowards the block. He saw the frightful boy precariously standing on the ledge, crying and grabbing onto a laundry pole. Mr Dipto raised the boom lifts platform towards the boy while calmly assuring the boy that he was there to rescue him. Within minutes, Mr Dipto reached out with both his arms, lifted the boy onto the platform and lowered him to safety, much to the relief and rousing cheers from a crowd of onlookers.When SCDF resources arrived, the boy had already been rescued. He was assessed by an SCDF paramedic and he did not require any medical assistance.Today, for their quick-thinking and selfless act, Mr Dipto and Mr Jibom received SCDF's Community Lifesaver Award from COL Lim Han Chee, 3rd SCDF Division Commander.Thank you Mr Dipto and Mr Jibom! Your commendable act brings us closer to building ANationOfLifesavers.

This allowed the CFRs to have the working space needed to safely administer CPR and use the AED. caption: [ ]Since SCDF took over marine firefighting operations in April 2012, SCDFs Marine Division has been growing steadily both in terms of capacity building and infrastructural development. In a short span of eight years, SCDFs Marine Division has grown from two firefighting vessels and a single marine fire station @ West Coast, to establishing a Marine Division Headquarters and a marine fire station @ Brani, a marine fire post @ Loyang and @ Gul. The Marine Division also acquired new, multi-purposed vessels, which can carry out prolonged and complex firefighting and rescue operations, including responding to a Chemical, Biological and Radiological incident at sea.To date, SCDFs Marine Fire Stations have responded to a number of fire and rescue operations, such as the Jalan Samulun fire in 2013 that resulted from an explosion on-board a tugboat where SCDF rescued four casualties; and in July 2018, SCDF marine firefighting resources battled a fire in the upper decks of the superstructure of a container ship in a 5-hour long firefighting operation. More recently on 13th November 2020, SCDFs Heavy Rescue Vessel and Rapid Response Fire Vessel were dispatched to rescue a man who had fallen down a hatch onboard a container vessel and had sustained a serious leg injury.The establishment and growth of the Marine Division was made possible, thanks to the dedicated officers of the Marine Division, led by Marine Commander, Assistant Commissioner (AC) Derek Tan. Today, the helm of SCDFs marine capabilities was handed over to Colonel (COL) Ryan Ong, the newly appointed Marine Commander, who was previously the Deputy Commander of the Marine Division.AC Derek Tan will assume his new appointment as Director Fire Safety Department.With Singapore as one of the worlds busiest ports, SCDF will keep innovating and enhancing our marine capabilities and continuously upgrade the skillsets of our marine officers to ensure prompt and effective emergency response to incidents within Singapores territorial waters.

caption: [Marine Rescue Operation @ Southeast of Singapore]At 12.30pm yesterday, SCDF received a call for medical assistance from an anchored container vessel in the southeast of Singapore. A man had fallen down a hatch onboard the container vessel and sustained a serious leg injury. Two SCDF marine vessels were deployed to the incident. Arriving alongside the container vessel, two SCDF marine specialists who are cross-trained as Emergency Medical Technicians quickly boarded the vessel with their rescue and medical equipment to assess the situation. A man was found conscious but immobile at the container vessels medical bay. As this was a case of fall, the SCDF marine specialists proceeded with great caution in handling the casualty and carefully secured him onto a stretcher. Concurrently, officers from SCDFs Heavy Rescue Vessel (HRV) boarded the container vessel to set up a lowering system of ropes and pulleys between the two vessels. This is an intricate rescue cum evacuation operation in view of the waves and windy condition out at sea. The casualty was safely lowered to the HRV's deck.He was then swiftly ferried to Marina South Pier where an SCDF emergency ambulance had been on standby to receive him. After a further medical assessment by the ambulance crew, he was conveyed to the Singapore General Hospital.

cleaned_caption: Fire Safety Tips for Use of Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) cylinders at Home. As we stay home during this period, some of us may be cooking our own meals. RESCUE INCIDENT at ALEXANDRA RD  
At 2.49pm, SCDF was alerted to a rescue incident at 378, Alexandra Road. 2 Fire Engines, 1 Red Rhino, 2 Firebikes, 1 ambulance and 3 supporting vehicles were dispatched to the incident site. Upon SCDF's arrival, a single-storey building (approx. 20m by 10m) fitted with a zinc roof had collapsed after a tree, approximately 15m in height and 3m in diameter, fell onto it. As a result, two casualties were trapped under the rubble. SCDF firefighters together with DART rescuers immediately commenced rescue operations after stabilising the fallen tree and the building structure. The search and rescue operation had to be conducted cautiously by delicately creating space within the collapsed structure using hydraulic cutting and lifting equipment. The first casualty was rescued in about 40 mins while the second casualty, who was pinned under the concrete debris, was extricated about 45 mins later. SCDF paramedics as well as a medical team from Alexandra Hospital were at the location to render medical assistance to both casualties. The casualties were sent to Alexandra Hospital by SCDF ambulance. The whole search and rescue operation took about 90 mins.
